items.title: Rate law form
items.description: Part (i) writes the differential rate equation as rate = k[A]^1[B]^2 (or dx/dt = k[A][B]^2) with [A] to the first power, [B] squared, and a rate constant k or K present.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Omitting rate constant k' foresees writing Rate = [A][B]^2 without k.
provenance.discriminates: A response that writes the rate law without any proportionality constant.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Core answer to sub-question (i); 0 discrimination but essential for correctness.

validation.gold_why: Rate constant K multiplies concentration terms.

items.title: Part ii ninefold
items.description: Part (ii) states that when the concentration of B is tripled, the rate becomes 9 times the original rate.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (ii) target: multiplicative factor; reference gives r1 = 9 × r0.
provenance.discriminates: A response that gives 3× (linear scaling) or any other factor.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Correct final result for (ii); caught 1/2 negatives, proving discriminative power.

validation.gold_why: States r1 = 9 × r0 when B is tripled.

items.title: Part ii 3B squared
items.description: Part (ii) shows the substitution of [3B] into the rate equation and evaluates 3^2 = 9 to obtain the rate multiplier.

provenance.evidence_detail: Reference shows r1 = k[A]^1[3B]^2 then r1 = 9 × r0; rollouts stated only the final factor.
provenance.discriminates: A response that asserts 9× without any substitution or derivation.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Key intermediate step; caught 1/2 negatives showing it separates correct from flawed.

validation.gold_why: Shows K[A]^1[3B]^2 yielding factor of 9.

items.title: Part iii eightfold
items.description: Part (iii) states that when the concentration of both A and B is doubled, the rate becomes 8 times the original rate.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (iii) target: multiplicative factor; reference gives r2 = 8 × r0.
provenance.discriminates: A response that gives 4×, 6×, or any factor other than 8.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Correct final result for (iii); caught 1/2 negatives, proving discriminative power.

validation.gold_why: States r2 = 8 × r0 when both doubled.

items.title: Part iii substitution
items.description: Part (iii) shows the new rate expression substituting [2A]^1 and [2B]^2 to derive the factor of 8.

provenance.evidence_detail: Reference shows r2 = k[2A]^1[2B]^2 then r2 = 8 × r0.
provenance.discriminates: A response that asserts 8× without showing the substitution into the rate law.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Required intermediate substitution; caught 1/2 negatives in validation.

validation.gold_why: Shows K[2A]^1[2B]^2 deriving factor of 8.

items.title: Part iii factors
items.description: Part (iii) computes the combined rate factor as 2^1 × 2^2 = 8, multiplying the per-reactant contributions rather than adding them.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Adding instead of multiplying factors' foresees 2 + 4 = 6.
provenance.discriminates: A response that adds the individual factors to get 6×.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Load-bearing arithmetic; caught 1/2 negatives, directly distinguishes correct reasoning.

validation.gold_why: Result 8 implies 2^1 × 2^2 multiplication.

items.title: Part ii A held
items.description: Part (ii) keeps the concentration of A unchanged and only varies [B] when computing the new rate.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (ii) specifies only [B] is tripled; reference keeps [A]^1 fixed.
provenance.discriminates: A response that also changes [A] in part (ii).
provenance.calibration_rationale: Implicit constraint of (ii); 0 discrimination but guards against a real conceptual error.

validation.gold_why: A concentration kept same; only B tripled.

items.title: Part ii baseline
items.description: Part (ii) writes an original rate expression r0 = k[A][B]^2 as the baseline before applying the tripling of B.

provenance.evidence_detail: Reference explicitly writes r0 = K[A]^1[B]^2 before r1.
provenance.discriminates: A response that jumps to the final factor without stating the baseline rate.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Adds derivational depth; 0 discrimination, low priority.
provenance.merged_mirror_text: Part (iii) writes an original rate expression r0 = k[A][B]^2 as the baseline before applying the doubling of A and B.

validation.gold_why: Writes r0 = K[A]^1[B]^2 as baseline.

items.title: dx/dt notation
items.description: Part (i) expresses the rate using dx/dt or equivalent time-derivative notation for the rate of reaction.

provenance.evidence_detail: Reference uses dx/dt notation; rollouts used 'rate' or -d[A]/dt instead.
provenance.discriminates: A response that gives only an expression like k[A][B]^2 with no indication it is a rate.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Notation depth from reference; 0 discrimination, purely optional.

validation.gold_why: Uses dx/dt notation for rate.

items.title: K or k accepted
items.description: Part (i) uses either K (capital) or k (lowercase) for the rate constant in the differential rate equation.

provenance.evidence_detail: Reference uses capital K; rollouts use lowercase k; both are conventional.
provenance.discriminates: A response that uses no constant symbol at all.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Notation flexibility; 0 discrimination, minor point.

validation.gold_why: Uses capital K for rate constant.

items.title: Avoid 3x in ii
items.description: Avoids stating in part (ii) that tripling the concentration of B increases the rate by 3× instead of 9×.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Linear not exponential for B' (severity high).
provenance.discriminates: A response that applies the concentration change linearly because B is second order.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Direct wrong-answer trap for (ii); caught 1/2 negatives in testing.

validation.gold_why: States 9× not 3× for tripling B.

items.title: Avoid adding in iii
items.description: Avoids computing the part (iii) rate change as 2^1 + 2^2 = 6 instead of 2^1 × 2^2 = 8.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Adding instead of multiplying factors' (severity high).
provenance.discriminates: A response that sums the individual order contributions.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Arithmetic operator trap for (iii); caught 1/2 negatives in testing.

validation.gold_why: Uses multiplication not addition; 8 not 6.

items.title: Avoid 4x in iii
items.description: Avoids computing the part (iii) rate change as 2 × 2 = 4 by ignoring the reaction orders of A and B.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Linear scaling for both reactants' (severity medium).
provenance.discriminates: A response that treats both reactants as first order and multiplies 2 by 2.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Order-ignoring trap for (iii); 0 discrimination but distinct from the addition error.

validation.gold_why: Result is 8 not 4.

items.title: Part iii factors multiplied
items.description: Part (iii) computes the combined factor as 2^1 × 2^2 = 8, multiplying the per-reactant contributions rather than adding them.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Adding instead of multiplying factors' foresees 2 + 4 = 6.
provenance.discriminates: A response that adds the individual factors to get 6×.

validation.gold_why: Result 8 implies 2^1 × 2^2 multiplication.

validation_summary.pitfall_weight_convention: stored on the RaR -1/-2 scale by schema.Criterion; graded by magnitude with polarity=positive

items.title: IP final value
items.description: The response reports the ionization potential IP of X as 11.835 eV (accepting 11.84 eV).

provenance.evidence_detail: Required deliverable for sub-question a; reference gives a = 11.835 eV.
provenance.discriminates: A response giving IP = 1.18 eV or 15.19 eV or any other wrong value.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 2/2 negatives; final requested quantity, correctness depends on it.

validation.gold_why: Reports a = IP = 11.835 eV.

items.title: EA final value
items.description: The response reports the electron affinity EA of X as 3.358 eV (accepting 3.36 eV).

provenance.evidence_detail: Required deliverable for sub-question b; reference gives b = 3.358 eV.
provenance.discriminates: A response giving EA = 0.336 eV or 6.71 eV or any other wrong value.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 2/2 negatives; final requested quantity, correctness depends on it.

validation.gold_why: Reports b = EA = 3.358 eV.

items.title: Step 1 energy balance
items.description: The response writes the step 1 energy balance for the transfer of one electron between the two halves of atoms as (N/2)×(IP − EA) = 409 kJ, with EA subtracted because electron attachment releases energy.

provenance.evidence_detail: Reference and correct rollouts use IP − EA for step 1; pitfall EA-sign-in-step-1 addresses the wrong move of adding EA.
provenance.discriminates: A response that writes (N/2)×(IP + EA) = 409 kJ or signs EA incorrectly.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 0/2 negatives but load-bearing equation; absorbed avoidance of EA-as-positive-cost.

validation.gold_why: Writes (N/2)(a−b) = 409 kJ step; EA subtracted.

items.title: Step 2 energy balance
items.description: The response writes the step 2 energy balance for converting X⁻ ions to X⁺ as (N/2)×(IP + EA) = 733 kJ, because removing the extra electron costs +EA and ionizing the neutral costs +IP.

provenance.evidence_detail: Reference uses a + b for step 2; pitfall Step-2-electron-count and EA-sign-in-step-2 address the wrong moves.
provenance.discriminates: A response that models X⁻ → X⁺ as one-electron removal costing only IP, giving (N/2)×IP = 733 kJ.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 1/2 negatives; combined with avoidance of EA-as-release-in-step-2 pitfall.

validation.gold_why: Writes (N/2)(a+b) = 733 kJ step; EA added.

items.title: Two-electron removal
items.description: The response states that converting each X⁻ ion to X⁺ requires removing two electrons: one reversing the electron affinity (costing +EA) and one the ionization of X (costing +IP).

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Step 2 electron count', severity high.
provenance.discriminates: A response that treats X⁻ → X⁺ as a single-electron transition costing only IP.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 1/2 negatives; key physical reasoning, absorbed one-electron-model pitfall.

validation.gold_why: States X⁻ loses two electrons: +EA then +IP.

items.title: Uses N/2 not N
items.description: The response uses N/2 = 3.0115×10²³ as the number of electron-transfer pairs in each energy-balance equation, not the full Avogadro's number N = 6.023×10²³.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Using N instead of N/2', severity medium; reference uses N/2 throughout.
provenance.discriminates: A response that plugs full N into both equations, halving all per-atom eV values.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 0/2 negatives but essential for correct scaling; absorbed using-full-N pitfall.

validation.gold_why: Uses N/2 in both energy-balance equations.

items.title: kJ to J conversion
items.description: The response converts the given energies to joules as 409×10³ J and 733×10³ J before dividing by N/2 and converting to eV.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'kJ to J omitted', severity medium.
provenance.discriminates: A response that uses 409 and 733 directly in J, making final values too small by 1000×.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 0/2 negatives but necessary unit step; absorbed dropping-kJ-to-J pitfall.

validation.gold_why: Uses 409×10³ and 733×10³ (J conversion).

items.title: eV conversion factor
items.description: The response uses the conversion 1 eV = 1.602×10⁻¹⁹ J to convert per-atom joule energies into eV.

provenance.evidence_detail: Reference explicitly divides by 1.602×10⁻¹⁹ to obtain eV.
provenance.discriminates: A response that omits this conversion or uses an incorrect factor.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 0/2 negatives but necessary for obtaining correct eV values.

validation.gold_why: Divides by 1.602×10⁻¹⁹ to convert to eV.

items.title: IP minus EA intermediate
items.description: The response obtains the intermediate value IP − EA = 8.477 eV from the 409 kJ step.

provenance.evidence_detail: Reference gives a − b = 8.477; rollout 3 wrongly obtained 0.8476 due to an exponent error.
provenance.discriminates: A response that reports IP − EA = 0.8476 eV or any value other than ~8.48 eV.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 1/2 negatives; load-bearing intermediate result for solving the system.

validation.gold_why: Obtains a−b = 8.477 eV.

items.title: IP plus EA intermediate
items.description: The response obtains the intermediate value IP + EA = 15.194 eV from the 733 kJ step.

provenance.evidence_detail: Reference gives a + b = 15.194; rollout 3 wrongly obtained 1.5194.
provenance.discriminates: A response that reports IP + EA = 1.5194 eV or any value other than ~15.19 eV.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 2/2 negatives; critical intermediate, both flawed responses missed it.

validation.gold_why: Obtains a+b = 15.194 eV.

items.title: Avoids exponent slip
items.description: Avoids writing the per-atom energy for the 409 kJ step as ~1.358×10⁻¹⁹ J; the correct per-atom value obtained by dividing 409×10³ by N/2 is ~1.358×10⁻¹⁸ J.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Exponent in J/eV conversion', severity medium, observed in rollout 3.
provenance.discriminates: A response containing the off-by-10 exponent error that propagates to all final values.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 1/2 negatives; observed arithmetic error in exponent of per-atom energy.

validation.gold_why: No per-atom value written incorrectly; correct method used.

items.title: Both quantities reported
items.description: The response reports both IP and EA values in eV for the atoms of X, explicitly labelled, rather than stopping after solving only one of the two.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Only one quantity reported', severity low; answer format demands two labelled values.
provenance.discriminates: A response that gives only IP or only EA.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 0/2 negatives; adds completeness check beyond individual values.

validation.gold_why: Reports both a (IP) and b (EA) in eV.

items.title: Simultaneous equations solved
items.description: The response solves the two simultaneous equations (IP − EA = 8.477 and IP + EA = 15.194) to obtain IP and EA, e.g. by adding and subtracting the two equations.

provenance.evidence_detail: Reference explicitly solves the system to reach a = 11.835 and b = 3.358.
provenance.discriminates: A response that fails to combine the two balances into solved IP and EA values.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 2/2 negatives; both flawed responses failed to solve the system.

validation.gold_why: Solves simultaneous equations for a and b.

items.title: Full expression for IP−EA
items.description: The response writes the full substituted expression (409×10³×2)/(1.602×10⁻¹⁹×6.023×10²³) for IP − EA, showing all constants.

provenance.evidence_detail: Reference gives a − b = 8.477; rollout 3 wrongly obtained 0.8476 due to an exponent error.
provenance.discriminates: A response that reports IP − EA = 0.8476 eV or any value other than ~8.48 eV.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Extends item 9 to verify computational setup; grounds the 8.477 result.

validation.gold_why: Obtains a−b = 8.477 eV.

items.title: Full expression for IP+EA
items.description: The response writes the full substituted expression (733×10³×2)/(1.602×10⁻¹⁹×6.023×10²³) for IP + EA, showing all constants.

provenance.evidence_detail: Reference gives a + b = 15.194; rollout 3 wrongly obtained 1.5194.
provenance.discriminates: A response that reports IP + EA = 1.5194 eV or any value other than ~15.19 eV.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Extends item 10 to verify computational setup; grounds the 15.194 result.

validation.gold_why: Obtains a+b = 15.194 eV.

validation_summary.pitfall_weight_convention: stored on the RaR -1/-2 scale by schema.Criterion; graded by magnitude with polarity=positive

items.title: Final potential 0.172 V
items.description: The response reports the one-electron electrochemical reaction potential as 0.172 V.

provenance.evidence_detail: Reference answer gives ε = 0.172 V as the single final result.
provenance.discriminates: A response that gives 0.158 V, 0.000172 V, -0.172 V, or no numerical answer.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Core answer; despite 0/3 discrimination, value is inseparable from correctness.

validation.gold_why: Reports ε = 0.172 V.

items.title: Positive sign from negation
items.description: The response reports E with a positive sign, consistent with negating ΔG = -εnF where ΔG = -16.6 kJ is negative, rather than producing -0.172 V.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Sign of E reversed' (high severity).
provenance.discriminates: A response that reports E = -0.172 V due to dropping the leading negative.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Sign correctness is a key algebraic step; 0/3 but no near-duplicate positive item exists.

validation.gold_why: Reports positive 0.172 V.

items.title: Single potential reported
items.description: The response reports a single potential value (0.172 V) as the answer rather than presenting two potentials as required output.

provenance.evidence_detail: Reference scope: reference gives a single derived quantity and dismisses ΔG°.
provenance.discriminates: A response that presents both 0.158 V and 0.172 V as co-equal answers.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 3/3 negatives; presenting E° alongside E was a common flawed-response error.

validation.gold_why: Reports single value 0.172 V.

items.title: Uses non-standard ΔG
items.description: The response uses ΔG = -16.6 kJ as the free energy input for computing the electrochemical potential.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts correctly used the right free energy for the main calculation; this criterion pins the correct choice against the wrong one.
provenance.discriminates: A response that uses ΔG° = -15.2 kJ instead, yielding 0.158 V.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Selecting the correct ΔG is essential to the answer; 0/3 but foundational to correctness.

validation.gold_why: Uses ΔG = -16,600 J from -16.6 kJ.

items.title: ΔG° is a distractor
items.description: The response states that ΔG° = -15.2 kJ does not matter for the asked-for potential because the non-standard ΔG governs it.

provenance.evidence_detail: Reference answer explicitly states 'The value of ΔG° does not matter.'
provenance.discriminates: A response that treats both free energies as required inputs for two separate potentials.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 3/3 negatives; explicit distractor recognition had maximum discrimination.

validation.gold_why: States ΔG° does not matter.

items.title: Applies ΔG = -nFE
items.description: The response applies the relation ΔG = -nFE (or ΔG = -εnF) to relate Gibbs free energy to the one-electron electrochemical potential.

provenance.evidence_detail: Reference answer opens with ΔG = -ε nF as the governing formula.
provenance.discriminates: A response that uses E = ΔG/(nF) without the leading negative, or uses an unrelated formula.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Load-bearing formula; 0/3 discrimination but required for a valid derivation.

validation.gold_why: States ΔG = -εnF.

items.title: n = 1 electron
items.description: The response sets n = 1 for the one-electron reaction in E = -ΔG/(nF), avoiding n = 2 or omission of n.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts identified n = 1 from the one-electron condition.
provenance.discriminates: A response that uses n = 2, giving 0.086 V, or omits n.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Absorbed avoidance of n error; correct n is a required intermediate.

validation.gold_why: Uses 1 mol e⁻ for n.

items.title: Converts kJ to joules
items.description: The response converts ΔG = -16.6 kJ to -16,600 J before dividing by Faraday's constant, avoiding a 0.000172 V unit slip.

provenance.evidence_detail: Consensus correct claim: -16.6 kJ = -16600 J before computation.
provenance.discriminates: A response that divides 16.6 directly by F, giving 0.000172 V.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Absorbed unit-slip avoidance; intermediate step with moderate importance.

validation.gold_why: Converts to -16,600 J.

items.title: Faraday constant value
items.description: The response uses Faraday's constant F = 96,500 C/mol e⁻ in the calculation of the electrochemical potential.

provenance.evidence_detail: Reference answer writes 96,500 C/mol e⁻.
provenance.discriminates: A response that uses F with mismatched or unspecified units affecting dimensional consistency.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 2/3 negatives; correct F with mol e⁻ units had strong measured discrimination.

validation.gold_why: Uses C/mol e⁻ units.

items.title: Shows rearrangement
items.description: The response writes E = -ΔG/(nF) or the equivalent rearrangement showing negation of the ΔG = -16.6 kJ input.

provenance.evidence_detail: Reference answer shows -16,600 J = -ε(1)(96,500), making the sign handling explicit.
provenance.discriminates: A response that jumps to 0.172 V without showing the sign inversion step.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Adds derivation transparency; 0/3 but real intermediate for a complete solution.

items.title: Substitution shown
items.description: The response substitutes -16,600 J, n = 1, and F = 96,500 C/mol e⁻ into ε = -ΔG/(nF).

provenance.evidence_detail: Reference answer explicitly substitutes -16,600 = -ε(1)(96,500).
provenance.discriminates: A response that gives the final number without the substitution.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Verifiable intermediate work; 0/3 but anchors the computation for grading.

validation.gold_why: Substitutes all values into equation.

items.title: Labels as ε or E
items.description: The response labels the final 0.172 V result as ε, E, or an equivalent potential symbol.

provenance.evidence_detail: Reference answer labels the result ε; question asks for 'the potential.'
provenance.discriminates: A response that reports 0.172 V without identifying what quantity it represents.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Minor labeling convention; 0/3 but quick to verify from any response.

validation.gold_why: Labels result as ε.

items.title: Avoids E° from ΔG°
items.description: Avoids reporting a standard potential E° = 0.158 V computed from ΔG° = -15.2 kJ as the required answer.

provenance.evidence_detail: All three rollouts computed E° = 0.158 V unnecessarily; reference says ΔG° does not matter.
provenance.discriminates: A response that presents E° = 0.158 V as part of the answer alongside or instead of 0.172 V.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 3/3 negatives; using ΔG° instead of ΔG was the dominant observed error.

validation.gold_why: No E° = 0.158 V reported.

items.title: Avoids Nernst conflation
items.description: Avoids Nernst-equation manipulation combining ΔG° = -15.2 kJ and ΔG = -16.6 kJ for the electrochemical potential rather than directly inverting ΔG = -nFE.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Nernst-style conflated use' (medium severity).
provenance.discriminates: A response that derives a confused pair of potentials from a ΔG − ΔG° = RT ln Q manipulation.
provenance.calibration_rationale: 0/3 observed but names a specific, checkable wrong approach; low weight.

validation.gold_why: Directly inverts ΔG = -εnF.

validation_summary.pitfall_weight_convention: stored on the RaR -1/-2 scale by schema.Criterion; graded by magnitude with polarity=positive

items.title: General speed formula
items.description: The response uses the general acoustic relation v = (K/ρ)^{1/2} connecting the wave speed to the bulk modulus and volumic mass density.

provenance.evidence_detail: All attempts and the reference agree on this starting formula; it is the load-bearing intermediate for both limits.
provenance.discriminates: A response that jumps to final answers without relating them to K and ρ, making the derivation uncheckable.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Foundational formula; 0/2 discrimination but necessary intermediate for all speed results.

validation.gold_why: Uses v = (K/ρ)^{1/2} as general acoustic relation.

items.title: General impedance formula
items.description: The response uses the general acoustic impedance relation Z = (Kρ)^{1/2} or equivalently Z = ρv, connecting impedance to bulk modulus and density.

provenance.evidence_detail: All attempts and the reference agree on Z = (Kρ)^{1/2} = ρv; it is the load-bearing intermediate for both impedance results.
provenance.discriminates: A response that uses an inverted impedance formula such as Z = v/ρ or Z = 1/(ρv).
provenance.calibration_rationale: Foundational formula; 0/2 discrimination but necessary intermediate for all impedance results.

validation.gold_why: Uses Z = (Kρ)^{1/2} as general impedance relation.

items.title: Isothermal bulk modulus derivation
items.description: The response uses the ideal-gas equation of state P = NT/V under isothermal conditions to derive the isothermal bulk modulus K = P.

provenance.evidence_detail: Part (i) requires the isothermal bulk modulus as an intermediate to derive v_T and Z_T.
provenance.discriminates: A response that uses K = γP for the isothermal case, swapping the two limits.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Key intermediate; 0.50 discrimination, load-bearing for isothermal speed and impedance.

validation.gold_why: States K = P for isothermal process explicitly.

items.title: Adiabatic bulk modulus derivation
items.description: The response uses the adiabatic relation P ∝ V^{−γ} (i.e., PV^γ = const) to derive the adiabatic bulk modulus K = γP.

provenance.evidence_detail: Part (ii) requires the adiabatic bulk modulus as an intermediate to derive v_S and Z_S.
provenance.discriminates: A response that uses K = P (no γ factor) for the adiabatic case.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Key intermediate; 0.50 discrimination, load-bearing for adiabatic speed and impedance.

validation.gold_why: States K = γP for adiabatic process explicitly.

items.title: Isothermal wave speed
items.description: The response gives the isothermal acoustic wave speed as v = (P/ρ)^{1/2}, equivalently (T/m)^{1/2}, where ρ is the volumic mass density.

provenance.evidence_detail: Part (i) explicitly asks for the wave speed in the isothermal limit; the reference gives v_T = (P/ρ)^{1/2} = (T/m)^{1/2}.
provenance.discriminates: A response that omits the isothermal speed or gives a wrong expression such as (γP/ρ)^{1/2}.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Directly requested quantity; 0.50 discrimination, essential to the answer.

validation.gold_why: Gives v = (P/ρ)^{1/2} = (T/m)^{1/2} for isothermal.

items.title: Isothermal wave impedance
items.description: The response gives the isothermal wave impedance as Z = (Pρ)^{1/2}, equivalently (mT)^{1/2}n where n is the particle density.

provenance.evidence_detail: Part (i) explicitly asks for the wave impedance in the isothermal limit; all consensus attempts and the reference agree on Z_T = (Pρ)^{1/2}.
provenance.discriminates: A response that computes only the wave speed and never evaluates the impedance, or gives an inverted formula such as Z = 1/(ρv).
provenance.calibration_rationale: Directly requested quantity; 0.50 discrimination, essential to the answer.

validation.gold_why: Gives Z = (Pρ)^{1/2} = (mT)^{1/2}n for isothermal.

items.title: Adiabatic wave speed
items.description: The response gives the adiabatic acoustic wave speed as v = (γP/ρ)^{1/2}, equivalently (γT/m)^{1/2}, where γ = C_P/C_V.

provenance.evidence_detail: Part (ii) explicitly asks for the wave speed in the adiabatic limit; the reference gives v_S = (γP/ρ)^{1/2} = (γT/m)^{1/2}.
provenance.discriminates: A response that drops the γ factor, writing v_S = (P/ρ)^{1/2} and making it identical to the isothermal case.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Directly requested quantity; 0.50 discrimination, essential to the answer.

validation.gold_why: Gives v = (γP/ρ)^{1/2} = (γT/m)^{1/2} for adiabatic.

items.title: Adiabatic wave impedance
items.description: The response gives the adiabatic wave impedance as Z = (γPρ)^{1/2}, equivalently (γmT)^{1/2}n.

provenance.evidence_detail: Part (ii) explicitly asks for the wave impedance in the adiabatic limit; all consensus attempts and the reference agree on Z_S = (γPρ)^{1/2}.
provenance.discriminates: A response that omits the adiabatic impedance entirely or drops the γ factor from it.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Directly requested quantity; 0.50 discrimination, essential to the answer.

validation.gold_why: Gives Z = (γPρ)^{1/2} = (γmT)^{1/2}n for adiabatic.

items.title: Adiabatic exceeds isothermal
items.description: The response states that the adiabatic wave velocity and impedance are larger than the isothermal values by a factor of γ^{1/2}, because γ > 1.

provenance.evidence_detail: Consensus among attempts and reference that v_S/v_T = Z_S/Z_T = sqrt(γ) > 1; the reference explicitly says adiabatic values are always larger.
provenance.discriminates: A response that claims the two limits give equal results or that isothermal values are larger.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Perfect 1.00 discrimination; central comparative result linking both limits.

validation.gold_why: States adiabatic v and Z are larger than isothermal by γ>1.

items.title: Adiabatic index definition
items.description: The response defines γ = C_P/C_V and states that γ > 1 for the ideal classical gas with temperature-independent specific heat.

provenance.evidence_detail: All attempts correctly identified γ = C_P/C_V > 1, and this is load-bearing for the adiabatic results and the comparison between limits.
provenance.discriminates: A response that uses γ ≤ 1 or never defines γ, making the comparison between limits unjustified.
provenance.calibration_rationale: 0/2 discrimination but necessary for correctness; defines the key parameter γ.

validation.gold_why: Defines γ = C_P/C_V and states γ > 1.

items.title: High frequency is adiabatic
items.description: The response identifies the adiabatic limit as the one achieved at higher wave frequencies, explaining that the oscillation period is too short for heat exchange.

provenance.evidence_detail: Part (iii) asks which limit is achieved at higher frequencies; the reference states the adiabatic result is realistic at usual sound frequencies.
provenance.discriminates: A response that assigns the isothermal limit to high frequencies, inverting the thermal-relaxation argument.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Directly answers the frequency sub-question; 0.50 discrimination, essential.

validation.gold_why: Identifies adiabatic as high-frequency limit; too fast for heat exchange.

items.title: Low frequency is isothermal
items.description: The response states that the isothermal process is the low-frequency limit, where the wave's period is long enough for temperature to equilibrate.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference specifies the isothermal case is implemented only at extremely low frequencies where the period allows temperature equilibration over the system size.
provenance.discriminates: A response that correctly names the high-frequency limit but never explains why the other limit is low-frequency.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Complements the high-frequency answer; 0.50 discrimination, important reasoning.

validation.gold_why: States isothermal is low-frequency limit with temperature equilibration.

items.title: Isothermal speed independent of compression
items.description: The response notes that the isothermal wave speed v = (T/m)^{1/2} does not depend on the static compression or ambient pressure of the gas.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference explicitly states 'v does not depend on the static compression of the gas,' a physical observation no attempt made.
provenance.discriminates: A response that treats v_T as depending on ambient pressure or density changes.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Reference-only depth; 0.50 discrimination, adds physical insight without being required.

validation.gold_why: Notes isothermal v does not depend on static compression.

items.title: Avoid frequency-regime reversal
items.description: Avoids claiming that the isothermal limit is achieved at higher wave frequencies or that the adiabatic limit is a low-frequency phenomenon.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Frequency–regime reversal' (severity high): inverting which limit corresponds to high vs low frequency.
provenance.discriminates: A response that swaps the frequency assignments, saying fast oscillations allow temperature equilibration.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Specific reversal trap; 0.50 discrimination, directly mirrors the frequency sub-question.

validation.gold_why: Correctly assigns adiabatic to high frequency, isothermal to low.

items.title: Avoid swapped or omitted gamma
items.description: Avoids using K = P for the adiabatic case, using K = γP for the isothermal case, or writing the adiabatic speed or impedance without the γ factor.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Swapped bulk modulus' (severity high): mixing up which thermodynamic variable is held constant in ∂P/∂V.
provenance.discriminates: A response that interchanges the two limits' bulk moduli, yielding v_T = v_S and Z_T = Z_S with wrong assignments.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Most common mistake family; 0.50 discrimination each, covers swapped modulus and omitted gamma.

validation.gold_why: Uses correct bulk modulus for each case, no swap.

validation_summary.pitfall_weight_convention: stored on the RaR -1/-2 scale by schema.Criterion; graded by magnitude with polarity=positive

items.title: Equal concentrations simplification
items.description: States that since the initial concentrations of two reactants A and B are equal and stoichiometry is 1:1, [A] = [B] throughout the reaction.

provenance.evidence_detail: Load-bearing simplification required by the reference answer to reduce the mixed second-order rate law to simple second-order form.
provenance.discriminates: A response that applies the general mixed-order formula without recognizing the equal-concentration edge case.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 1/2 negatives; foundational reasoning that enables correct simplification.

validation.gold_why: States concentrations start equal and remain equal throughout.

items.title: Second-order treatment
items.description: Identifies the reaction as second order overall (first order with respect to each reactant) and treats it as a simple second order reaction with rate = k[A]^2.

provenance.evidence_detail: All correct rollouts and the reference reduce the mixed second-order rate law to the simple second-order form using equal concentrations.
provenance.discriminates: A response that keeps the mixed second-order form and divides by zero, or that uses a first-order law.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 1/2 negatives; key step connecting overall order to one-variable treatment.

validation.gold_why: Treats as simple second order, uses integrated law.

items.title: Integrated rate law form
items.description: Writes the integrated rate law as 1/[A] = 1/[A]_0 + kt with the plus sign before the kt term, using the initial concentration [A]_0 = 0.100 mol and k = 1.0 × 10^{-2}.

provenance.evidence_detail: Consensus among all correct rollouts and the reference answer uses the form 1/[A] = 1/[A]_0 + kt.
provenance.discriminates: A response that writes 1/[A] = 1/[A]_0 - kt, producing an increasing concentration.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 2/2 negatives; correct equation with plus sign is essential to the answer.

validation.gold_why: Writes 1/[A] = kt + 1/[A_0] with correct values.

items.title: Reciprocal of initial concentration
items.description: Computes the reciprocal of the initial concentration as 1/[A]_0 = 1/0.100 = 10.0 L/mol.

provenance.evidence_detail: All correct rollouts and the reference compute 1/[A]_0 = 10.0 L/mol as an intermediate value.
provenance.discriminates: A response that mishandles the reciprocal of 0.100 M.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 1/2 negatives; load-bearing intermediate value 10.0 L/mol.

validation.gold_why: Shows 1/0.100 mol, sum implies 10.0 L/mol.

provenance.evidence_detail: Given value of k must appear in the response's calculation to reach the correct answer.
provenance.discriminates: A response that alters the value of k (e.g., treating it as a first-order constant with different units).
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 1/2 negatives; load-bearing intermediate value kt = 1.0 L/mol.

validation.gold_why: Uses k = 1.0 × 10^{-2} in calculation.

items.title: Uses given time
items.description: Uses t = 100 s as the elapsed time in the integrated rate law computation.

provenance.evidence_detail: Given time value is required to compute kt = 1.0 L/mol.
provenance.discriminates: A response that substitutes a different time value into the integrated law.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 0/2 negatives; confirms correct input but lower discrimination.

validation.gold_why: Uses t = 100 s in calculation.

items.title: Sum to 11 L/mol
items.description: Computes 1/[A] = 10.0 + 1.0 = 11 L/mol.

provenance.evidence_detail: All correct rollouts and the reference obtain 1/[A] = 11 L/mol before taking the reciprocal.
provenance.discriminates: A response that sums to a different value (e.g., 9.0, 10.1, 11.0 reported as final answer).
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 2/2 negatives; essential intermediate sum directly determines final answer.

validation.gold_why: Explicitly states = 11 L/mol.

items.title: Final concentration 0.091 M
items.description: Reports the concentration of A remaining as the reciprocal of 11 L/mol, i.e., [A] = 0.091 M, rather than reporting 11 L/mol as the concentration.

provenance.evidence_detail: This is the required final deliverable: concentration of A remaining after 100 s.
provenance.discriminates: A response that reports 11 M or 11 L/mol as the concentration, or that gives 0.037 M from a first-order law.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 2/2 negatives; final answer 0.091 M is the required result.

validation.gold_why: Reports [A] = 0.091 M.

items.title: Units of M
items.description: States the final concentration of A with units of M (mol/L).

provenance.evidence_detail: Question demands the concentration of A remaining, with implied units of M.
provenance.discriminates: A response that omits units or reports L/mol as the final concentration unit.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 0/2 negatives; correct units add precision but are lower priority.

validation.gold_why: Final answer given as 0.091 M.

items.title: Avoid first-order misapplication
items.description: Avoids using the first-order integrated law ln[A] = ln[A]_0 - kt with k = 1.0 × 10^{-2} as a pseudo-first-order constant, which would yield approximately 0.0368 M.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined high-severity pitfall: 'First-order law misapplied'.
provenance.discriminates: A response that misreads 'first order with respect to each reactant' as 'first order overall'.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 1/2 negatives; first-order trap observed in flawed responses.

validation.gold_why: No first-order integrated law used.

items.title: Avoid mixed-order division by zero
items.description: Avoids using the general mixed second-order integrated law (1/([B]_0-[A]_0))·ln([B][A]_0/([A][B]_0)) = kt with [A]_0 = [B]_0 = 0.100 M, which causes division by zero.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined medium-severity pitfall: 'Mixed-order formula with equal concentrations'.
provenance.discriminates: A response that reaches for the general mixed-order formula without simplifying for equal concentrations.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 0/2 negatives; genuine specific trap though not observed in test set.

validation.gold_why: Uses simple second-order law, not mixed-order.

validation_summary.pitfall_weight_convention: stored on the RaR -1/-2 scale by schema.Criterion; graded by magnitude with polarity=positive

items.title: Pellet mass
items.description: The response identifies the mass of the pellets as 5.7 g.

provenance.evidence_detail: Reference and all rollouts agree on mass = 5.7 g as a load-bearing input.
provenance.discriminates: A response that uses a different mass value or omits it entirely.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Necessary input but zero discrimination; both flawed responses included it.

validation.gold_why: States mass of pellets = 5.7 g clearly.

items.title: Displacement principle
items.description: The response states that the volume of the pellets equals the volume of water displaced, using the water level readings from the graduated cylinder.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference answer explicitly identifies the pellet volume as the volume of water displaced.
provenance.discriminates: A response that computes the right number without connecting it to the displacement principle.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Key conceptual step; caught 1/2 negatives, moderate discrimination.

validation.gold_why: States volume equals volume of water displaced.

items.title: Displaced volume
items.description: The response computes the volume of water displaced as 7.7 ml − 5.0 ml = 2.7 ml.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts and the reference agree the displaced volume is 2.7 ml; this is the core displacement step.
provenance.discriminates: A response that uses 7.7 ml, 5.0 ml, or a sum as the pellet volume.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Core intermediate; absorbed pitfall 6; caught 1/2 negatives.

validation.gold_why: Computes 7.7 - 5.0 = 2.7 ml explicitly.

items.title: Density formula
items.description: The response applies the density formula as mass divided by volume using 5.7 g / 2.7 ml.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference answer shows ρ = 5.7 g / 2.7 ml as the load-bearing ratio.
provenance.discriminates: A response that inverts the ratio to 2.7 / 5.7 or uses wrong operands.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Central calculation; absorbed pitfall 7; caught 2/2 negatives, perfect discrimination.

validation.gold_why: Applies density formula as 5.7 g / 2.7 ml.

items.title: Final density value
items.description: The response reports the density of the pellets as 2.1 g/ml.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Missing or wrong units' identifies omitting or mislabeling units as a failure mode.
provenance.discriminates: A response that reports 2.1 with no units or with units such as g or ml.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Final answer with correct units; caught 2/2 negatives, perfect discrimination.

validation.gold_why: Attaches units g/ml to the value 2.1.

items.title: Correct density units
items.description: The response attaches the units g/ml to the density value 2.1.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Missing or wrong units' identifies omitting or mislabeling units as a failure mode.
provenance.discriminates: A response that reports 2.1 with no units or with units such as g or ml.

validation.gold_why: Attaches units g/ml to the value 2.1.

items.title: N+1 states, energies
items.description: The response states that the only equilibrium configurations are n = 0, 1, …, N with the first n links open and the rest closed, each having energy E_n = nΔ and corresponding to a single microstate.

provenance.evidence_detail: Part (a) requires calculating ⟨n⟩; identifying the correct state space (N+1 states, no degeneracy) is the load-bearing first step that all consensus rollouts agreed on.
provenance.discriminates: Catches responses that treat the N links as independent two-state systems with 2^N configurations or C(N,n) degeneracy, which would produce a Fermi-Dirac-like result instead of the correct geometric-series partition function.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Core model setup; caught 2/2 negatives. Without correct state count the entire calculation fails.

validation.gold_why: States N+1 states with energy nΔ, single microstate each.

items.title: Geometric partition function
items.description: The response writes the partition function as the geometric progression Z = Σ_{n=0}^{N} e^{-nΔ/T} = (1 − λ^{N+1})/(1 − λ) with λ = e^{-Δ/T} < 1.

provenance.evidence_detail: All three rollouts and the reference agree on Z = (1−λ^{N+1})/(1−λ) with λ = e^{-Δ/T}.
provenance.discriminates: Catches responses that write Z = (1−λ^N)/(1−λ) (off-by-one, dropping the n=N term) or Z = (1+e^{-Δ/T})^N (independent links).
provenance.calibration_rationale: Closed-form Z is load-bearing; caught 2/2 negatives. Required for all downstream results.

validation.gold_why: Writes geometric progression with λ=e^{-Δ/T}<1.

items.title: Exact formula for ⟨n⟩
items.description: The response gives the exact closed-form formula ⟨n⟩ = 1/(e^{Δ/T} − 1) − (N+1)/(e^{(N+1)Δ/T} − 1).

provenance.evidence_detail: All three rollouts and the reference give this exact closed-form expression (Eq. (**)).
provenance.discriminates: Catches responses that drop the second term (N+1)/(e^{(N+1)Δ/T}−1), which would diverge as T/Δ at high temperature instead of saturating at N/2.
provenance.calibration_rationale: The central result; caught 2/2 negatives. Correctness collapses without it.

validation.gold_why: Exact formula given in equation (**).

items.title: Low-temperature limit
items.description: The response gives the low-temperature limit ⟨n⟩ ≈ e^{-Δ/T} ≪ 1 for T ≪ Δ, which is approximately independent of N.

provenance.evidence_detail: All three rollouts and the reference agree on this limit; the reference explicitly shows the second term is negligible for N > 1.
provenance.discriminates: Catches responses that claim the second term (N+1)e^{-(N+1)Δ/T} dominates at low T, or that give a different low-T scaling such as e^{-NΔ/T}.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Required limit for temperature dependence analysis; caught 1/2 negatives, so slightly lower.

validation.gold_why: States low-T limit e^{-Δ/T}, independent of N.

items.title: High-temperature limit
items.description: The response gives the high-temperature limit ⟨n⟩ ≈ N/2 valid when T ≫ (N+1)Δ.

provenance.evidence_detail: All three rollouts and the reference agree that ⟨n⟩ → N/2 at high temperature, where each link has equal probability of being open or closed.
provenance.discriminates: Catches responses that give N or N/2 − 1 as the high-T limit, or that claim ⟨n⟩ diverges without bound.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Key limiting behavior; caught 2/2 negatives. Essential for temperature dependence analysis.

validation.gold_why: States high-T limit ⟨n⟩≈N/2.

items.title: Intermediate regime T/Δ
items.description: The response identifies the intermediate temperature regime ⟨n⟩ ≈ T/Δ valid for Δ ≪ T ≪ NΔ when N ≫ 1.

provenance.evidence_detail: All three rollouts and the reference identify this linear regime, which the reference derives from the first term having reached T/Δ while the second remains negligible.
provenance.discriminates: Catches responses that give only two regimes (low-T and high-T) and miss the broad intermediate window where ⟨n⟩ grows linearly with T.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Nontrivial intermediate behavior for long chains; caught 1/2 negatives. Important but less central.

validation.gold_why: Identifies ⟨n⟩≈T/Δ for Δ≪T≪(N+1)Δ.

items.title: Crossover scale NΔ
items.description: The response states that the crossover temperature scale between linear growth and saturation at N/2 occurs at T ~ NΔ.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts and the reference identify T ~ NΔ (or equivalently (N+1)Δ) as the scale where the second term transitions from negligible to important.
provenance.discriminates: Catches responses that place the crossover at T ~ Δ, missing the N-dependence of the saturation scale.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Added depth on crossover; caught 1/2 negatives. Real insight but secondary to the main limits.

validation.gold_why: Crossover at T~(N+1)Δ implied by regime boundaries.

items.title: Derivative trick for numerator
items.description: The response computes the numerator sum Σ_{n=1}^{N} nλ^n using the derivative relation λ d/dλ Σ_{n=0}^{N} λ^n, where λ = e^{-Δ/T}.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference and all rollouts use λ ∂/∂λ to evaluate the weighted sum; the reference explicitly writes λ ∂/∂λ [(1−λ^{N+1})/(1−λ)].
provenance.discriminates: Catches responses that compute d/dλ[Σ λ^n] without the prefactor λ, which would introduce an erroneous factor of e^{Δ/T} into the result.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Key intermediate derivation step; caught 2/2 negatives. Required to reach the exact formula.

validation.gold_why: Uses λ d/dλ derivative trick for numerator.

items.title: Gibbs probability W_n
items.description: The response writes the Gibbs distribution probability W_n = e^{-nΔ/T}/Z for the state with n open links.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference writes W_n = (1/Z) exp{−nΔ/T} using Eqs. (2.58) and (2.59); all rollouts agree.
provenance.discriminates: Catches responses that assign equal probability to all states, or that use a degeneracy factor C(N,n) in the probability weight.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Foundational statistical mechanics step; caught 2/2 negatives. Precursor to computing ⟨n⟩.

validation.gold_why: Writes W_n = e^{-nΔ/T}/Z.

items.title: High-T equal probability
items.description: The response states that at high temperature the energy cost Δ is negligible so each link has approximately equal probability of being open or closed.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference states: 'at very high temperatures, the energy gain Δ is negligible, and each link has an equal chance to be open or closed.'
provenance.discriminates: Catches responses that give the N/2 limit numerically but do not explain the physical basis in terms of Δ becoming negligible relative to T.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Physical picture behind N/2 limit; caught 1/2 negatives. Adds intuition but not a required calculation.

validation.gold_why: States Δ negligible, equal open/closed probability.

items.title: Physical interpretation T/Δ
items.description: The response provides the physical interpretation that thermal agitation with characteristic energy T ≫ Δ opens on average T/Δ links but not more.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference states: 'the thermal agitation with the characteristic energy T ≫ Δ is sufficient to open, on average, T/Δ left links of the chain, but not more than that.'
provenance.discriminates: Catches responses that derive the T/Δ scaling mathematically but do not connect it to the physical picture of thermal energy opening links.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Explains the intermediate regime physically; caught 2/2 negatives. Adds required physical insight.

validation.gold_why: Gives physical interpretation of T/Δ links opened.

items.title: High-T condition (N+1)Δ
items.description: The response states that the high-temperature limit requires T to exceed both Δ and (N+1)Δ, not merely T ≫ Δ.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference explicitly states: 'If T is much larger than both Δ and (N+1)Δ' as the condition for the N/2 limit.
provenance.discriminates: Catches responses that state T ≫ Δ alone is sufficient for the N/2 saturation, which would incorrectly apply the high-T limit in the intermediate regime.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Critical condition often missed; caught 2/2 negatives. Prevents applying N/2 limit too broadly.

validation.gold_why: Requires T≫Δ and (N+1)Δ for high-T limit.

items.title: Ratio form of average
items.description: The response expresses the average ⟨n⟩ as the ratio Σ_{n=1}^{N} n e^{-nΔ/T} / Σ_{n=0}^{N} e^{-nΔ/T} before evaluating the closed form.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference writes ⟨n⟩ = Σ n W_n = [Σ n e^{-nΔ/T}] / [Σ e^{-nΔ/T}] as an intermediate step before computing the geometric sums.
provenance.discriminates: Catches responses that jump to the final answer without showing the ensemble average construction from the Gibbs distribution.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Intermediate expression before closed-form; caught 2/2 negatives. Shows correct setup of the average.

validation.gold_why: Expresses ⟨n⟩ as ratio of sums before closed form.

items.title: Large-N Bose-Einstein form
items.description: The response states that for N ≫ 1 at fixed temperature T, the second term becomes negligible and ⟨n⟩ approaches 1/(e^{Δ/T} − 1).

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts note the large-N limit.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Directly addresses 'especially for N≫1'; caught 2/2 negatives. Central to the question's focus.

validation.gold_why: Second term negligible for N≫1, approaches Bose-Einstein form.

items.title: Avoids binomial degeneracy
items.description: Avoids treating the equilibrium chain as N independent two-level systems with 2^N states or C(N,n) binomial degeneracy.

provenance.evidence_detail: Part (a) requires calculating ⟨n⟩; identifying the correct state space (N+1 states, no degeneracy) is the load-bearing first step that all consensus rollouts agreed on.
provenance.discriminates: Catches responses that treat the N links as independent two-state systems with 2^N configurations or C(N,n) degeneracy, which would produce a Fermi-Dirac-like result instead of the correct geometric-series partition function.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Primary trap for this problem; caught 2/2 negatives via the positive companion item.

validation.gold_why: States N+1 states with energy nΔ, single microstate each.

items.title: Classifies as paucibacillary

items.title: Single lesion supports PB

provenance.calibration_rationale: Key clinical reasoning; caught 1/2 negatives, anchors PB diagnosis to presentation.

validation.gold_why: Cites single hypopigmented lesion supporting PB.

items.title: Negative smear supports PB

items.title: Rifampicin 600 mg monthly

items.title: Clofazimine 300 mg monthly
items.description: The response states or endorses T-clofazimine 300 mg once a month as part of the selected regimen.

items.title: Correction formula and substitution
items.description: States the correction formula X_dot_C = X_dot(P/P_C)(T_C/T) and shows the full numerical substitution as (100)(760/591.6)(293/309).

provenance.discriminates: A response that uses an inverted or rearranged formula (e.g., X_dot_C = X_dot(P_C/P)(T/T_C)) would produce wrong ratios.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 2/2 negatives; the formula and its full substitution are the core derivation.

validation.gold_why: Formula X_dot_C = X_dot(P/P_C)(T_C/T) shown.

items.title: Pressure ratio orientation
items.description: Computes the pressure ratio as 760 torr divided by 591.6 torr with 760 in the numerator.

provenance.evidence_detail: All correct rollouts place 760 over 591.6; the mined pitfall 'Pressure ratio inverted' identifies 591.6/760 as a high-severity error.
provenance.discriminates: A response that inverts the pressure ratio (591.6/760) would get approximately 73.8 mR/hr instead of 121.8.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 1/2 negatives; reversing the pressure ratio is a common error in this problem.

validation.gold_why: 760/591.6 with 760 in numerator.

items.title: Temperature ratio orientation
items.description: Computes the temperature ratio as 293 K divided by 309 K with 293 in the numerator.

provenance.evidence_detail: All correct rollouts place 293 over 309; the mined pitfall 'Temperature ratio inverted' identifies 309/293 as a high-severity error.
provenance.discriminates: A response that inverts the temperature ratio (309/293) would get approximately 135.5 mR/hr instead of 121.8.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 1/2 negatives; reversing the temperature ratio is a common error in this problem.

validation.gold_why: 293/309 with 293 in numerator.

items.title: Temperature conversions
items.description: Converts the calibration temperature as (273 + 20) = 293 K and the measurement temperature as (273 + 36) = 309 K.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference and all rollouts perform this conversion explicitly; the mined pitfall 'Celsius used instead of Kelvin' identifies using 20 directly as a high-severity error.
provenance.discriminates: A response that uses 20 instead of 293 would compute a wrong temperature ratio (~71.4 mR/hr).
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 0/2 negatives but necessary intermediate quantities for the final result.

items.title: Base exposure rate used
items.description: Uses 100 mR/hr as the base exposure rate X_dot in the correction calculation.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts and the reference use X_dot = 100 mR/hr as the starting value in the formula.
provenance.discriminates: A response that uses a different base value or omits it from the computation would get a different result.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 0/2 negatives; the given field strength is a required input to the formula.

validation.gold_why: Uses 100 mR/hr as base rate.

items.title: Current equality derivation
items.description: Derives the correction by equating the measurement and calibration currents, stating I = I_C because the detector response is matched.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts and the reference use the condition I = I_C to derive X_dot_C = X_dot(P/P_C)(T_C/T).
provenance.discriminates: A response that does not invoke I = I_C may use an unjustified or incorrectly derived correction formula.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 0/2 negatives; the I = I_C step is the key reasoning linking the two regimes.

validation.gold_why: States I = I_C to derive correction.

items.title: Detector current equation
items.description: States the detector current equation I = K multiplied by X_dot multiplied by (P/T), where K is a constant for a given detector.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts and the reference derive the correction from I = K·X_dot·(P/T), which is the starting equation of the scenario.

provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 0/2 negatives; the underlying equation is needed to justify the correction.

validation.gold_why: I = K X_dot (P/T) stated.

provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 0/2 negatives; distinguishing P_C from P prevents using the wrong pressure.

validation.gold_why: 591.6 torr identified as P_C.

items.title: Final ⟨U⟩ formula
items.description: States the final expression for the mean internal energy as \(\langle U \rangle = \frac{\partial(\beta F)}{\partial\beta}\), avoiding both a spurious negative sign and the omission of the additive \(F\) term.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Sign of mean energy' (high severity, foreseen): the chain of two minus signs tempts an incorrect overall negative sign.
provenance.discriminates: A response that writes ⟨U⟩ = -∂(βF)/∂β anywhere in the derivation, even if the final answer is later corrected.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Core result; gold=pass. Absorbs two avoidance items for the same formula.

validation.gold_why: Uses positive sign, not negative.

items.title: Final ⟨S⟩ formula
items.description: States the final entropy expression as \(\langle S \rangle = \beta^2 \frac{\partial F}{\partial \beta}\) with no explicit \(k_B\) or \(k\) factor multiplying this formula and with the correct power of \(\beta\).

provenance.evidence_detail: All three rollouts included an explicit Boltzmann constant (k_B or k) in ⟨S⟩ = k_B β² ∂F/∂β, but the reference gives ⟨S⟩ = β² ∂F/∂β with k absorbed into β.
provenance.discriminates: A response that writes ⟨S⟩ = k_B β² ∂F/∂β or ⟨S⟩ = k β² ∂F/∂β, which every rollout did.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Core result; gold=pass, caught 3/3 negatives, discrimination=1.00.

validation.gold_why: States ⟨S⟩ = β² ∂F/∂β with no k_B factor.

items.title: ln Z_N = −βF relation
items.description: States or uses the relation \(\ln Z_N = -\beta F\) (equivalently \(F = -\frac{1}{\beta}\ln Z_N\)) connecting the canonical partition function to the free energy.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (c) requires derivation from Z_N = e^{-βF}; all rollouts used this relation and consensus_correct confirms it.
provenance.discriminates: A response that attempts the derivation without ever invoking the link between Z_N and F.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Load-bearing identity linking partition function to free energy; gold=FAIL but derivationally essential.

validation.gold_why: Relation ln Z_N = -βF not mentioned.

items.title: Derivative of Z_N
items.description: Shows the intermediate derivative step \(\frac{\partial Z_N}{\partial\beta} = -\sum_{\phi} E[\phi]\, e^{-\beta E[\phi]}\) obtained by differentiating the sum over configurations.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (c) requires showing steps; all rollouts performed this differentiation as the first step of the derivation.
provenance.discriminates: A response that jumps straight to the final formula without showing how differentiating Z_N produces the energy-weighted sum.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Required intermediate; low discrimination (0/3) but derivationally necessary.

validation.gold_why: Intermediate derivative of Z_N not shown.

items.title: ⟨U⟩ via ln Z_N
items.description: Shows the intermediate form \(\langle U \rangle = -\frac{\partial \ln Z_N}{\partial\beta}\), connecting the derivative of the log of the canonical partition function to the mean internal energy.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (c) requires derivation steps; consensus_correct confirms all rollouts derived this identity correctly.
provenance.discriminates: A response that states ⟨U⟩ = ∂(βF)/∂β without showing the prior step through -∂ ln Z_N/∂β.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Key bridging step between partition function and free energy; derivationally essential.

validation.gold_why: Form ⟨U⟩ = -∂ ln Z_N/∂β not shown.

items.title: Product rule expansion
items.description: Expands \(\frac{\partial(\beta F)}{\partial\beta}\) using the product rule to obtain \(F + \beta\frac{\partial F}{\partial\beta}\) as the expression for the mean internal energy.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (c) requires showing steps; the product rule expansion is the link from -∂ ln Z_N/∂β to ∂(βF)/∂β.
provenance.discriminates: A response that writes ∂(βF)/∂β as the final answer but never shows the F + β ∂F/∂β expansion.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Load-bearing algebraic step producing the final ⟨U⟩ form.

validation.gold_why: Product rule expansion not shown.

items.title: Thermodynamic identity for S
items.description: Uses the thermodynamic relation \(F = \langle U \rangle - T\langle S \rangle\) (i.e., \(\langle S \rangle = \frac{\langle U \rangle - F}{T}\)) as the starting point for deriving the entropy expression.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (b) requires deriving ⟨S⟩ from F = U - TS; consensus_correct confirms all rollouts used this structure.
provenance.discriminates: A response that derives ⟨S⟩ from a different starting point or simply states the entropy formula without using F = ⟨U⟩ - T⟨S⟩.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Required starting point for entropy derivation; links free energy and entropy.

validation.gold_why: Thermodynamic identity for S not used.

items.title: Intermediate ⟨S⟩ and substitution
items.description: Shows the intermediate expression \(\langle S \rangle = \beta(\langle U \rangle - F)\) and then substitutes \(\langle U \rangle - F = \beta\frac{\partial F}{\partial\beta}\) to obtain \(\langle S \rangle = \beta^2 \frac{\partial F}{\partial\beta}\).

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (c) requires showing steps; the intermediate ⟨S⟩ = β(⟨U⟩ - F) bridges the thermodynamic identity to the statistical expression.
provenance.discriminates: A response that jumps from F = ⟨U⟩ - T⟨S⟩ directly to ⟨S⟩ = β² ∂F/∂β without showing the intermediate rearrangement.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Both steps caught 3/3 negatives, discrimination=1.00; critical substitution chain.

validation.gold_why: Intermediate ⟨S⟩ form not shown.

items.description: The derivation explicitly performs the substitution x=ka with dk=dx/a, transforming the integral to ∫_{−π}^{π} δ(E−E_s+2J cos x) dx.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts show x=ka, dk=dx/a, and the integral transformed to limits [−π, π].
provenance.discriminates: A response that keeps k as the integration variable and mishandles the limits or the Jacobian dk=dx/a.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 2/2 negatives, disc=1.00; necessary intermediate eliminating a from the integral.

validation.gold_why: No substitution x=ka shown in reference

items.title: Delta identity
items.description: The identity δ(g(k)) = Σ_i δ(k−k_i)/|g'(k_i)| is stated for handling the delta function of a composite argument in the integral.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts use this standard identity to decompose the delta function at its roots.
provenance.discriminates: A response that evaluates δ(g(k)) without identifying the roots or applying the Jacobian factor.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 1/2 negatives, disc=0.50; key identity converting the delta into a sum over roots.

validation.gold_why: Delta-of-function identity not stated

items.title: Jacobian value
items.description: The Jacobian |g'(k_i)| = √(4J²−(E−E_s)²) is derived at each root of the delta function argument.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts compute |g'(x_i)| = 2|J|√(1−cos²x₀) = √(4J²−(E−E_s)²).
provenance.discriminates: A response that computes the Jacobian as 2J sin(ka₀) without the absolute value or the simplification to the sqrt form.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 2/2 negatives, disc=1.00; produces the square-root denominator of the final expression.

validation.gold_why: Jacobian not explicitly derived in reference

items.title: Delta-derivative relation
items.description: The relationship δ(y) = dθ(y)/dy is stated as the basis for transforming the delta function integral into terms involving the Heaviside function.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts cite δ(y) = dθ(y)/dy to connect the delta function integral to Heaviside step functions.
provenance.discriminates: A response that uses θ in the final answer without explaining its connection to the delta function.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 1/2 negatives, disc=0.50; directly answers how the delta is transformed into theta.

validation.gold_why: δ=dθ/dy relationship not stated

items.title: Integration-differentiation
items.description: The explanation describes how integrating the Heaviside step function over k-space and then differentiating with respect to E yields the density of states expression.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts explain that δ(g(k)) = (d/dE)θ(g(k)), so integrating θ over k and differentiating w.r.t. E produces n(E).
provenance.discriminates: A response that gives the final formula but provides no explanation of the δ-to-θ transformation procedure.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 2/2 negatives, disc=1.00; central to the second sub-question on the transformation.

validation.gold_why: No integration-differentiation explanation given

items.title: Root condition
items.description: The root condition cos(ka₀) = −(E−E_s)/(2J) is explicitly stated for the argument of the delta function in the integral.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts state cos x₀ = −(E−E_s)/(2J) as the equation g(x)=0.
provenance.discriminates: A response that solves for the root incorrectly or does not state the condition on cos(ka₀).
provenance.calibration_rationale: Real intermediate step; disc=0.00 but anchors the two-root structure of the integral.
provenance.merged_mirror_text: The function g(k) = E−E_s + 2J cos(ka) is explicitly identified as the argument of the Dirac delta function in the integral.

validation.gold_why: Root condition not stated in reference

items.title: Band edges defined
items.description: The band-edge energies E_b and E_t corresponding to E−E_s = ±2J are defined in the derivation of the expression involving the Heaviside function.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference uses E_b and E_t in the step function arguments; rollouts express this as |E−E_s| ≤ 2|J| instead.
provenance.discriminates: A response that writes θ(E−E_b)−θ(E−E_t) without defining E_b and E_t.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Needed for the theta support boundaries; disc=0.00, gold=FAIL, so weighted low.

validation.gold_why: E_b and E_t used but not defined

items.title: Derivative g'(k)
items.description: The derivative g'(k) = −2Ja sin(ka) is explicitly computed for the argument g(k) = E−E_s + 2J cos(ka) of the delta function.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts compute g'(x) = −2J sin x as the derivative needed for the Jacobian.
provenance.discriminates: A response that skips computing g'(k) and cannot justify the Jacobian factor.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Concrete intermediate preceding the Jacobian; disc=0.00 but specific to this integral.

validation.gold_why: g'(k) not computed in reference

items.title: Avoids single root
items.description: Avoids counting only one root of the delta function argument within [−π/a, π/a] instead of the two symmetric roots ±k₀ that each contribute 1/|g'(k_i)|.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Counting only one root' (severity high): forgetting the second root at −k₀ halves the result.
provenance.discriminates: A response that identifies only k₀ = arccos[−(E−E_s)/(2J)] and misses −k₀, yielding N/(π√(4J²−(E−E_s)²)) instead of 2N/(π√(4J²−(E−E_s)²)).
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 1/2 negatives, disc=0.50; missing the second root halves the result.

validation.gold_why: Expression accounts for both roots symmetrically

items.title: Avoids wrong ordering
items.description: Avoids the wrong band-edge ordering in the theta function expression θ(E−E_b)−θ(E−E_t) where E_b > E_t for J > 0, which evaluates to −1 inside the band.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Wrong band-edge ordering' (severity medium): the reference uses E_b, E_t without defining them, and the bottom/top assignment depends on the sign of J.
provenance.discriminates: A response that defines E_b = E_s + 2J and E_t = E_s − 2J for J > 0, reversing the step-function difference and giving a negative DOS.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Real sign trap in the theta support; disc=0.00 but specific to this question's form.

validation.gold_why: Uses standard θ(E−E_b)−θ(E−E_t) form

items.title: Pion max momentum
items.description: The maximum momentum of the π− in the laboratory is stated as approximately 79 MeV/c (or equivalently ~80 MeV/c).

provenance.evidence_detail: Reference answer gives p_π = 79 MeV/c; consensus of rollouts gives ~79.9 MeV/c.
provenance.discriminates: A response that reports the unboosted rest-frame momentum p* ≈ 39 MeV/c or a wrongly boosted value.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Core answer; gold-pass, caught 2/2 negatives, perfect discrimination.

validation.gold_why: States 79 MeV/c for pion.

items.title: Lab equals c.m. frame
items.description: The response identifies that the laboratory frame coincides with the c.m. frame for this colliding beam at c.m. energy 4.03 GeV.

provenance.evidence_detail: Implicit constraint in the question structure; no extra boost is needed between c.m. and lab for the D* production stage.
provenance.discriminates: A response that treats the lab as a fixed-target frame or applies an unnecessary boost to the D*.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Necessary assumption; gold-FAIL, zero discrimination but conceptually required.

items.title: Unequal-mass formula
items.description: The D∗− energy in the c.m. frame is computed using the unequal-mass two-body formula E_D* = (s + m_{D*}² − m_{D+}²)/(2√s) with √s = 4.03 GeV, rather than the equal-mass formula.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Equal-mass production formula' shows using √(s/4 − m²) gives ~160 MeV/c instead of ~550 MeV/c.
provenance.discriminates: A response that uses the symmetric equal-mass formula and gets p_D* ≈ 160 MeV/c.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Key formula; caught 1/2 negatives with 0.50 discrimination.

items.title: D* energy intermediate
items.description: The D∗− energy in the c.m. frame is computed as approximately 2082 MeV.

provenance.evidence_detail: Consensus of rollouts gives E_D* ≈ 2082.5 MeV; this is the load-bearing intermediate for the boost parameters.
provenance.discriminates: A response that gets a different D* energy and therefore wrong boost parameters.

items.title: Correct D0bar mass
items.description: The D∗− decays kinematics use the D̄0 mass 1863.3 MeV/c², not the D+ mass 1868.3 MeV/c².

provenance.discriminates: A response that uses 1868.3 MeV/c² in the D* → D̄0 + π decay and gets p* ≈ 13.5 MeV/c.
provenance.calibration_rationale: High discrimination: caught 2/2 negatives; using wrong mass changes decay kinematics.

validation.gold_why: Mass usage not shown in reference answer.

items.title: Pion rest-frame p*

items.title: Pion rest-frame energy
items.description: The pion energy in the D∗− rest frame is computed as approximately 144.9 MeV.

items.title: Forward emission

items.title: Lorentz boost formula
items.description: The maximum pion lab momentum is obtained via the Lorentz boost p_π = γ(p* + βE*_π), using both the pion rest-frame momentum and rest-frame energy.

provenance.evidence_detail: Consensus of rollouts applies γ(p* + βE*_π) ≈ 1.037 × (38.9 + 0.264 × 144.9) ≈ 80 MeV/c.

provenance.calibration_rationale: Key formula; caught 1/2 negatives; errors here cascade to wrong answer.

validation.gold_why: Boost formula not shown in reference.

items.title: D* boost beta
items.description: The velocity parameter β of the D∗− in the c.m. frame is computed as approximately 0.264.

provenance.evidence_detail: Consensus of rollouts gives β ≈ 0.2640 from E_D* and m_{D*} = 2008.6 MeV/c².
provenance.discriminates: A response that computes a different β and therefore boosts the pion incorrectly.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Optional intermediate; caught 1/2 negatives.

validation.gold_why: Beta not stated in reference answer.

items.title: D* boost gamma
items.description: The Lorentz factor γ of the D∗− in the c.m. frame is computed as approximately 1.037.

provenance.calibration_rationale: Optional intermediate; caught 1/2 negatives.

validation.gold_why: Gamma not stated in reference answer.

items.title: Avoids rest-frame stop
items.description: Avoids reporting the final pion lab momentum as the D∗− rest-frame value p* ≈ 39 MeV/c without applying the Lorentz boost to the laboratory frame.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Stopping one step early': reporting p* ≈ 38.9 MeV/c as the final answer instead of ~79 MeV/c.
provenance.discriminates: A response that computes p* correctly but reports it as the lab-frame maximum.

items.title: Avoids cross-frame sum
items.description: Avoids obtaining the maximum pion lab momentum by adding the D∗− lab momentum (~550 MeV/c) directly to the pion rest-frame momentum p* (~39 MeV/c).

items.title: Avoids massless boost

items.title: Full logical chain
items.description: Explicitly connects the definition to the conclusion that since E_gs < 0, the zero potential level at E = 0 lies above the ground state and is therefore excited.

items.description: Notes that for the zero potential level to be classified as an excited state, E = 0 must correspond to an actual energy eigenvalue of the Hamiltonian, not merely an arbitrary reference point.

items.title: Potential sets spectrum

provenance.discriminates: A response that claims shifting the potential changes which state is ground or excited.

items.title: Arbitrariness acknowledged
items.description: Acknowledges that the zero of potential energy is an arbitrary reference choice but notes that once fixed, the relative ordering of eigenvalues has physical implications.

provenance.discriminates: A response that either ignores the arbitrariness entirely or uses it to dismiss the question.

items.description: Acknowledges that if E = 0 lies at a continuum threshold rather than being a discrete eigenvalue, the zero level may not be a normalizable excited bound state.

provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 2/2 negatives; advanced nuance about eigenvalue nature of E=0.

validation.gold_why: Continuum caveat not addressed.

items.title: Avoids potential-as-state
items.description: Avoids classifying V(x) = 0 as a ground or excited state without reference to the Hamiltonian eigenvalue problem and without E = 0 being a genuine energy eigenvalue.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Potential vs. eigenvalue confusion' (severity: high): only eigenvalues of H, not values of V, are classified.

provenance.calibration_rationale: Disc 0.00 but covers a distinct QFT localization sub-question; kept for coverage.

validation.gold_why: QFT localization not discussed.

items.title: Position eigenstates
items.description: States that position eigenstates satisfy ⟨x|x'⟩ = δ(x−x') and are non-normalizable distributions rather than physical quantum states of the electron, so the superposition must use finite-width states rather than |x₁⟩ + |x₂⟩.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Position eigenstate as physical' (severity medium): responses may use non-normalizable position kets as realizable states.
provenance.discriminates: A response that writes |x₁⟩ + |x₂⟩ as the electron's state without acknowledging these are not physical states.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Disc 1.00; technical correction that both flawed responses missed.

validation.gold_why: Does not write superposition as point-eigenstate sum.

items.title: Finite-width wavepackets
items.description: States that physical localized states of the electron are finite-width wavepackets ψ_A(x), ψ_B(x) rather than point-localized states.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (d) and implicit constraint: physical localized states must be superpositions of wavepackets, not disjoint point locations.
provenance.discriminates: A response that implies an electron can be localized to an exact mathematical point.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Disc 1.00; positive complement to the position-eigenstate correction.

validation.gold_why: Finite-width wavepackets not mentioned.

items.title: Born rule probability
items.description: States the Born rule gives the probability of finding the electron in region R as P(R) = ∫_R |ψ(x)|² dx.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (d) and consensus_correct: all rollouts included Born rule probability density.

validation.gold_why: Born rule not mentioned.

items.title: Unitary evolution vs measurement
items.description: States that the electron's wavefunction evolves unitarily according to the Schrödinger equation between measurements, and distinguishes this unitary evolution from the definite outcome obtained upon measurement of the electron.

provenance.discriminates: A response that discusses superposition without mentioning unitary Schrödinger evolution.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Disc 0.50 from source 20; conceptual backbone of the measurement problem.

validation.gold_why: Schrödinger equation not mentioned.

items.title: Double-slit detection
items.description: Describes the double-slit experiment with electrons where each individual electron is detected as a single localized dot and the interference pattern emerges statistically over many single-electron detection events, one dot at a time.
