validation.gold_why: Interference cross term not included.

items.title: Which-path interference loss

items.title: Reaction order 1.5
items.description: States the reaction order as 1.5.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts gave n = 3, but the reference answer gives n = 1.5 using the formula n = [log(a2/a1) + log(t1/t2)] / log(t1/t2).
provenance.discriminates: A response that correctly applies the standard proportionality method and gets n = 3 fails this criterion, which is the reference-required answer.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Core answer; caught 2/3 negatives, proven signal.

validation.gold_why: States n = 1.5 explicitly.

items.title: Rate constant unit
items.description: States the unit of the rate constant as lit^{-1/2} · mole^{-1/2} · min^{-1}.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts gave L^2·mol^{-2}·s^{-1} (consistent with n = 3), but the reference gives lit^{-1/2}·mole^{-1/2}·min^{-1} (consistent with n = 1.5).
provenance.discriminates: A response that derives the third-order unit L^2·mol^{-2}·s^{-1} instead of the reference's 3/2-order unit fails this criterion.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Requested quantity; caught 3/3 negatives, maximum discrimination.

validation.gold_why: States lit^{-1/2} · mole^{-1/2} · min^{-1}.

items.title: Log formula for order
items.description: Uses the formula n = [log(a2/a1) + log(t1/t2)] / log(t1/t2) where a1, a2 are initial concentrations and t1, t2 are half-life periods to find the reaction order.

validation.gold_why: Uses the specified formula with log terms.

items.title: Half-life factor nine
items.description: Identifies that the half-life increases by a factor of nine when the initial concentration is reduced.

provenance.evidence_detail: The problem states 'increase nine times'; this given must be extracted correctly as part of setting up the solution.
provenance.discriminates: A response that misreads the nine-fold increase as a decrease or uses a different factor would fail.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Problem given needed for setup; 0/3 but anchors the calculation.

validation.gold_why: States t_2 = 9 t_1.

items.title: Concentration one-third
items.description: Identifies that the initial concentration of the reactants is reduced to one-third.

provenance.evidence_detail: The problem states 'initial concentration ... reduced to one-third'; this given must be extracted correctly.
provenance.discriminates: A response that treats the concentration as reduced by one-third (i.e., to two-thirds) or uses a different ratio would fail.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Problem given needed for setup; 0/3 but anchors the calculation.

validation.gold_why: States a_2 = a_1/3.

items.title: Substitute concentration ratio
items.description: Substitutes the concentration ratio a2/a1 = 1/3 into the log formula for the reaction order.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference sets a2 = a1/3 and substitutes log(1/3) into the formula.
provenance.discriminates: A response that uses a2/a1 = 3 instead of 1/3 in the formula fails.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Required intermediate; caught 2/3 negatives, solid signal.

validation.gold_why: Substitutes 1/3 for a2/a1.

items.title: Substitute half-life ratio
items.description: Substitutes t2/t1 = nine (equivalently t1/t2 = 1/9) into the log formula for the reaction order.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference sets t2 = 9·t1 and substitutes log(1/9) into the formula.
provenance.discriminates: A response that uses t2/t1 = 1/9 in the numerator position incorrectly, or fails to connect the nine-fold factor to the formula, fails.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Required intermediate; caught 2/3 negatives, solid signal.

validation.gold_why: Substitutes 1/9 for t1/t2.

items.title: Intermediate ratio 1/2
items.description: Computes log(1/3)/log(1/9) = 1/2 as an intermediate step toward the reaction order n = 1.5.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference's computation yields this ratio, which when added to 1 gives n = 1.5.
provenance.discriminates: A response that computes log(1/9)/log(1/3) = 2 instead (the inverted ratio) would get n = 3 and fail this criterion.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Load-bearing intermediate; caught 3/3, gold=FAIL but genuinely needed.

validation.gold_why: Does not explicitly show log(1/3)/log(1/9) = 1/2.

items.title: Variable definitions
items.description: States that t1 and t2 denote half-life periods and a1 and a2 denote initial concentrations used in the log formula.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference explicitly defines t1 as the half-life at concentration a1 and t2 as the half-life at concentration a2.
provenance.discriminates: A response that substitutes numbers without defining which half-life and concentration correspond to which variable fails.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Clarifies formula usage; caught 2/3 negatives, moderate signal.

validation.gold_why: Defines t1, t2 as half-life periods, a1, a2 as concentrations.

items.title: Unit derivation
items.description: Derives the rate constant unit using the general unit formula with order n = 1.5.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference computes the unit lit^{-1/2}·mole^{-1/2}·min^{-1} from n = 1.5 via the general formula L^(n-1)·mol^(1-n)·time^{-1}.
provenance.discriminates: A response that states the correct unit but derives it from n = 3 instead of n = 1.5 fails.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Adds derivation depth; caught 2/3, gold=FAIL so kept low.

validation.gold_why: States unit but does not show derivation using n = 1.5.

items.title: Connects givens to order
items.description: Sets up an equation relating the nine-fold half-life increase to the one-third concentration reduction to solve for the reaction order.

provenance.evidence_detail: The core task is connecting these two given factors through the half-life proportionality to obtain the order.
provenance.discriminates: A response that lists both given factors but never writes an equation connecting them to solve for n fails.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Bridges givens to formula; 0/3 but needed for setup coverage.

validation.gold_why: Sets up equation relating nine-fold increase to one-third reduction.

items.title: Avoid exponent sign error
items.description: Avoids writing the half-life dependence as [A]^(n-1) instead of [A]^(1-n), which reverses the sign of the exponent.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Exponent sign error': using t½ ∝ [A]^(n-1) instead of [A]^(1-n) yields n = -1.
provenance.discriminates: A response that uses the wrong exponent sign obtains a negative reaction order or an otherwise inconsistent result.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Specific sign trap; 0/3 observed but low-magnitude pitfall.

validation.gold_why: No exponent sign error present.

items.title: Avoid n–1 as order
items.description: Avoids reporting n minus one as the reaction order instead of solving for n itself.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Stopping at n-1': the solver derives n-1 = 2 from 3^(n-1) = 3² but reports 2 as the order.
provenance.discriminates: A response that correctly sets up the equation but stops at n-1 = 2 and reports order 2 fails.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Trap of stopping early; 0/3 observed but low-magnitude pitfall.

validation.gold_why: Reports n = 1.5, not n-1.

items.title: Avoid ratio direction mix
items.description: Avoids mixing the half-life ratio direction (t1/t2 versus t2/t1) inconsistently with the concentration ratio (a2/a1).

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Half-life ratio direction': assigning t1/t2 = 9 while also using a2/a1 = 1/3 mixes directions and causes sign confusion.
provenance.discriminates: A response that uses t1/t2 = 9 together with a2/a1 = 1/3 fails because the ratios point in opposite directions.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Directional error trap; caught 1/3 negatives, real but modest.

validation.gold_why: Uses ratios consistently without direction mix.

items.title: Half-life concentration dependence
items.description: States that half-life depends on initial concentration, which is the basis for determining the reaction order.

provenance.evidence_detail: The underlying concept tested is the dependence of half-life on initial concentration as a diagnostic for order.
provenance.discriminates: A response that gives only numerical results without mentioning the half-life–concentration relationship provides less conceptual grounding.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Conceptual basis; gold=FAIL, 0/3, kept low as genuinely foundational.

validation.gold_why: Does not explicitly state half-life depends on concentration.

items.title: Correct verdict: No
items.description: States that no interference pattern will be observed at D2 without coincidence counting, even if 100% of the signal photons are detected at D1.

provenance.evidence_detail: Part (a) asks for a yes/no verdict on whether interference appears at D2 without coincidence counting; the reference answer and all three rollouts agree the answer is No.
provenance.discriminates: A response that answers 'Yes' or claims interference appears unconditionally at D2.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Discrimination 1.00, gold=pass; the verdict is the answer.

validation.gold_why: Directly states no interference without coincidence counting.

items.title: Entangled state formula
items.description: Writes the entangled signal–idler state as |Ψ⟩ = (1/√2)(|1⟩ᵢ|s₁⟩ₛ + |2⟩ᵢ|s₂⟩ₛ) with ⟨s₁|s₂⟩ ≈ 0, expressing the superposition of idler slit-path states entangled with the signal photon.

provenance.evidence_detail: All three rollouts write the joint state as |Ψ⟩ = (1/√2)(|1⟩ᵢ|s₁⟩ₛ + |2⟩ᵢ|s₂⟩ₛ) with ⟨s₁|s₂⟩ ≈ 0 as the starting point for the derivation.
provenance.discriminates: A response that writes an unentangled idler state or omits the correlation between idler paths and signal states.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Discrimination 1.00; concrete formula anchoring the entanglement argument.

validation.gold_why: Does not write entangled state superposition.

items.title: Entanglement yields mixed idler
items.description: Identifies that entanglement between the signal and idler photons causes the reduced idler state to be a mixed state rather than a pure state, encoding which-path information in the signal photon.

provenance.evidence_detail: All three rollouts agree that signal-idler entanglement destroys idler path coherence, yielding a mixed reduced state; this is the central explanatory claim for part (b).
provenance.discriminates: A response that treats the idler as remaining in a pure state after the signal is detected at D1.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Discrimination 0.50; key conceptual link between entanglement and loss of interference.

validation.gold_why: Does not mention entanglement causing mixed idler state.

items.title: Reduced density matrix
items.description: States the reduced density matrix of the idler as ρᵢ = ½(|1⟩⟨1| + |2⟩⟨2|) with zero off-diagonal coherence terms when the signal states are orthogonal.

provenance.evidence_detail: All three rollouts write ρᵢ = ½(|1⟩⟨1| + |2⟩⟨2|) with ⟨s₁|s₂⟩ ≈ 0 and zero off-diagonal terms; this intermediate formalism is load-bearing for the conclusion.
provenance.discriminates: A response that claims the off-diagonal terms of ρᵢ are nonzero or does not address the reduced density matrix structure.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Discrimination 1.00; specific mathematical anchor proving no interference.

validation.gold_why: Does not state reduced density matrix or off-diagonal terms.

items.title: Unconditioned D2 probability
items.description: Gives the unconditioned D2 detection probability as P(x) = ½(|ψ₁(x)|² + |ψ₂(x)|²) with no interference cross-term 2Re[ψ₁*ψ₂].

provenance.evidence_detail: All three rollouts give P_D2(x) = ½(|ψ₁(x)|² + |ψ₂(x)|²) with no interference cross-term, which is the key quantitative result showing no fringes.
provenance.discriminates: A response that writes the D2 probability with a nonzero cross-term, implying interference fringes.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Discrimination 1.00; shows mathematically why no interference pattern appears.

validation.gold_why: Does not give unconditioned D2 probability formula.

items.title: 100% detection ≠ coherence
items.description: States that 100% detection at D1 ensures every idler photon has a correlated signal record but does not restore off-diagonal density matrix terms or select a pure-state subensemble of the idler.

provenance.evidence_detail: All three rollouts state that perfect detection efficiency ensures every idler has a correlated signal record but does not select a coherent subensemble or restore path coherence.
provenance.discriminates: A response that claims 100% D1 detection alone is sufficient to produce interference at D2.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Discrimination 1.00; directly addresses the question's core misconception.

validation.gold_why: Does not discuss off-diagonal terms or pure-state subensemble.

items.title: Coincidence = postselection
items.description: Explains that coincidence counting corresponds to conditioning the idler counts at D2 on specific D1 measurement outcomes, i.e., postselection of conditional subensembles.

provenance.evidence_detail: All three rollouts explain that coincidence sorting selects conditional subensembles (quantum eraser) that can show fringes or anti-fringes.
provenance.discriminates: A response that treats coincidence counting as merely detecting pairs without sorting by D1 outcome.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Discrimination 0.50; clarifies why coincidence counting is necessary.

validation.gold_why: Does not explain coincidence counting as postselection.

items.title: Conditional fringes cancel
items.description: Explains that coincidence-selected conditional subensembles at D2 can show fringes and anti-fringes that are π out of phase and cancel exactly when summed over all D1 outcomes, yielding no net interference pattern without coincidence counting.

provenance.evidence_detail: All three rollouts explain that quantum eraser subensembles show fringes/anti-fringes which cancel when summed over all D1 outcomes.
provenance.discriminates: A response that argues since some coincidence channels show interference, the total D2 pattern must also show residual fringes.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Discrimination 1.00; explains the cancellation mechanism.

validation.gold_why: Does not mention conditional fringe cancellation.

items.title: Zero unconditioned visibility
items.description: States that the unconditioned fringe visibility at D2 is zero, so no interference pattern is observed at D2 without coincidence counting.

provenance.evidence_detail: Rollouts 2 and 3 explicitly state visibility = 0; rollout 1 implies it via the vanishing interference term.
provenance.discriminates: A response that claims nonzero residual visibility in the unconditioned D2 distribution.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Discrimination 1.00 but overlaps with the verdict; adds the visibility concept.

validation.gold_why: Does not explicitly state zero unconditioned visibility.

items.title: No-signaling principle
items.description: Invokes the quantum mechanical no-signaling principle to explain that the signal photon operations at D1 cannot change the marginal D2 distribution of idler photons.

provenance.evidence_detail: Rollout 2 explicitly invokes no-signaling; rollouts 1 and 3 mention it only implicitly. The reference is silent, so this is a supplementary argument.
provenance.discriminates: A response that claims operating D1 with 100% efficiency changes the local D2 interference pattern without addressing the no-signaling constraint.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Discrimination 1.00; adds deeper quantum-mechanical justification.

validation.gold_why: Does not invoke no-signaling principle.

items.title: Interference requires coherence
items.description: States that observing an interference pattern at D2 requires coherence between the amplitudes for the idler traversing slit 1 and slit 2 of the double slit.

provenance.evidence_detail: The question structure's implicit constraints state that interference at D2 requires coherence between the two path amplitudes; all rollouts invoke this condition.
provenance.discriminates: A response that claims interference can appear without coherence between the two slit amplitudes.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Discrimination 0.00 but directly answers the question's ask about conditions for interference.

validation.gold_why: Does not state interference requires path coherence.

items.title: Avoids collapse to pure state
items.description: Avoids claiming that measurement at D1 collapses the idler into a pure superposition state with restored path coherence, or computing the D2 probability by dropping entanglement and treating the idler as the pure state (1/√2)(|1⟩ + |2⟩).

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined high-severity pitfall 'Collapse yields pure superposition': assuming D1 measurement collapses the idler into a pure superposition with restored coherence.
provenance.discriminates: A response that states the idler's post-measurement state is pure and coherent, so off-diagonal terms ⟨1|ρᵢ|2⟩ are nonzero.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Discrimination 1.00 for both sources; two facets of the same collapse error.

validation.gold_why: Does not claim D1 collapses idler into pure superposition.

items.title: Avoids marginal as conditional

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined high-severity pitfall 'Marginal vs. conditional confusion': answering as though the question asks about the conditional D2 distribution rather than the unconditioned marginal.
provenance.discriminates: A response that claims interference appears at D2 by implicitly sorting idler counts on D1 outcomes while the question asks about the pattern without coincidence counting.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Discrimination 1.00; flags the conflation of marginal and conditional distributions.

validation.gold_why: Does not treat marginal as conditional distribution.

items.title: Avoids efficiency = coincidence
items.description: Avoids treating 100% D1 detection efficiency as functionally equivalent to performing coincidence counting and concluding all events are coincidence events.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined medium-severity pitfall 'Efficiency treated as postselection': reasoning that 100% D1 detection is equivalent to coincidence counting since no pair is lost.

validation.gold_why: Does not equate detection efficiency with coincidence counting.

provenance.discriminates: A response that claims the off-diagonal terms of ρᵢ are nonzero or does not address the reduced density matrix structure.

items.title: Reactivity from valence

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (b) asks how rules predict reactivity; this causal chain is the required reasoning.
provenance.discriminates: A response that states periodic trends predict reactivity without explaining the proton-to-electron-configuration link.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Required for reactivity sub-question; merged items, gold=FAIL, zero discrimination but essential coverage.

validation.gold_why: No link from Z to reactivity described.

items.title: Crystal from bonding
items.description: States that the crystal structure of an element is predicted from bonding type — metallic, covalent, or molecular — derived from proton number, naming at least one structure type such as FCC, BCC, HCP, covalent network, or molecular lattice.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (c) asks how rules predict crystal structure; consensus_correct confirms bonding-type-to-lattice mapping.
provenance.discriminates: A response that predicts crystal structure without connecting it to bonding type or proton number.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Required for crystal structure sub-question; merged items, gold=FAIL, zero discrimination but essential.

validation.gold_why: Crystal structure not discussed.

items.title: Other properties predicted
items.description: Includes prediction of properties such as melting point, density, conductivity, or nuclear decay mode from proton or neutron number.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (d) asks for prediction of other properties beyond reactivity and crystal structure.
provenance.discriminates: A response that covers only reactivity and crystal structure without mentioning any additional property.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Optional depth on other properties; gold=FAIL, zero discrimination, not load-bearing.

validation.gold_why: No specific properties predicted.

items.title: Specific examples given
items.description: Provides examples with specific elements or isotopes and their stated proton number Z and neutron number N to illustrate the rules.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (e) asks for concrete worked examples; divergent analysis shows rollouts used different examples but all included some.
provenance.discriminates: A response that discusses rules abstractly without applying them to any named element or isotope.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Question explicitly requests examples; gold=FAIL, zero discrimination but genuinely required.

validation.gold_why: No specific element or isotope examples given.

items.title: Limitations discussed
items.description: Discusses limitations of the rules, naming at least one specific failure mode such as exceptions to periodic trends, relativistic effects for heavy elements, dependence on external conditions, or kinetic isotope effects.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Missing isotopic effects limitation' notes that claiming isotopes are chemically identical in every respect is a foreseeable error.
provenance.discriminates: A response that states isotopes have zero chemical differences, ignoring measurable kinetic isotope effects.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Question explicitly requests limitations; merged 3 sources, gold=FAIL but genuinely necessary.

validation.gold_why: Isotope effects not mentioned.

items.title: Avoids N chemistry
items.description: Avoids attributing chemical reactivity or crystal structure to neutron number or nuclear stability rules such as band of stability instead of to proton number.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'N drives chemistry' (severity high) foresees responses claiming isotopic variation changes chemical reactivity or bonding type.
provenance.discriminates: A response that claims, for example, C-14 is more chemically reactive than C-12 due to its extra neutrons.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Specific conceptual trap; caught no negatives but addresses known chemistry/nuclear confusion.

validation.gold_why: Does not attribute chemistry to neutron number.

items.title: Avoids deterministic trends
items.description: Avoids stating periodic trends such as ionization energy or atomic radius as strict monotonic rules without any exceptions.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Trends as deterministic' (severity medium) foresees claims that ionization energy always increases left-to-right with no exceptions.
provenance.discriminates: A response that states ionization energy strictly increases across a period, ignoring the Group 2-to-13 and Group 15-to-16 drops.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Key conceptual error about trends; zero measured discrimination but traps common overgeneralization.

validation.gold_why: Does not state trends as strict monotonic rules.

items.title: Avoids deterministic crystal
items.description: Avoids presenting crystal structure as predictable from element identity alone without noting dependence on temperature, pressure, or allotropic and polymorphic forms.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Crystal structure deterministic' (severity medium) foresees claims like 'iron is always BCC' or 'carbon always forms diamond'.
provenance.discriminates: A response that assigns a single fixed lattice to each element without acknowledging phase transitions or polymorphism.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Crystal-specific overgeneralization; merged allotrope item, zero discrimination but covers key trap.

validation.gold_why: Does not present crystal structure as deterministic.

items.title: Avoids ionic lattice
items.description: Avoids using ionic compound radius-ratio rules such as CsCl or NaCl structure types as examples of predicting the crystal structure of an element.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Ionic lattices wrong scope' notes Rollout 3 used radius-ratio rules for binary ionic compounds to answer a question about elemental crystal structure.
provenance.discriminates: A response that answers the crystal-structure sub-question with cation-anion radius ratios instead of metallic or covalent packing.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Observed pitfall (caught 1/3 negatives); addresses misapplying ionic rules to pure elements.

validation.gold_why: No ionic lattice rules used.

validation_summary.pitfall_weight_convention: stored on the RaR -1/-2 scale by schema.Criterion; graded by magnitude with polarity=positive

items.title: Modulus-one determinant
items.description: The response states that for a unitary matrix, |det U|² = 1, or equivalently det U = e^{iα} where α is a real number.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (a) asks for the general constraint on det(U) for a unitary matrix; the reference derives |det U|² = 1 and det U = e^{iα}.
provenance.discriminates: A response that gives a wrong modulus (e.g., det U = 1) or omits the general property entirely.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Fundamental result; 0/2 discrimination but essential to the answer's correctness.

validation.gold_why: States |det U|² = 1 explicitly.

items.title: Starting identity det(UU†)
items.description: The response uses det(UU†) = det 1 = 1 as the starting point for deriving the determinant of a unitary matrix.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference explicitly shows the chain det(UU†) = det 1 = 1 and det U† = (det U)* leading to |det U|² = 1.
provenance.discriminates: A response that asserts |det U| = 1 without connecting it to the unitary condition UU† = I.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Key derivation step; 0/2 discrimination but load-bearing intermediate identity.

validation.gold_why: Derives from det(UU†)=1 and det U†=(det U)*.

items.title: Dagger determinant property
items.description: The response uses the property det U† = (det U)* in deriving |det U|² = 1.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference explicitly shows the chain det(UU†) = det 1 = 1 and det U† = (det U)* leading to |det U|² = 1.
provenance.discriminates: A response that asserts |det U| = 1 without connecting it to the unitary condition UU† = I.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Required intermediate step; 0/2 discrimination but necessary for the proof.

validation.gold_why: Derives from det(UU†)=1 and det U†=(det U)*.

items.title: Matrix-exponential identity
items.description: The response states det(exp(iF)) = exp(i Tr F) for the operator U = exp(iF).

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (b) asks to calculate det(U) explicitly for U = exp(iF); the reference gives det U = exp(i Tr F).
provenance.discriminates: A response that uses a wrong identity such as det(exp(A)) = exp(det A) or det(exp(A)) = Tr(exp A).
provenance.calibration_rationale: Core requested quantity; 0/2 discrimination but essential to the answer.

validation.gold_why: States det U = exp(i Tr F).

items.title: Eigenvalue sum form
items.description: The response expresses det U = exp(i Σ_k λ_k), where λ_k are the real eigenvalues of the Hermitian matrix F.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts express the determinant in terms of the eigenvalues of F as exp(i Σ λ_k); the question specifies F has a known spectrum.
provenance.discriminates: A response that writes the product of eigenvalues of F directly (e.g., λ_1·λ_2···λ_N) instead of the exponential of the sum.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Equivalent restatement; gold=FAIL and 0/2, so low weight but adds explicit eigenvalue detail.

validation.gold_why: Does not express det U = exp(i Σ λ_k) explicitly.

items.title: Hermitian real spectrum
items.description: The response states that since F is Hermitian, its eigenvalues λ_k are real, so i Tr F is purely imaginary and det U is a phase.

provenance.evidence_detail: Consensus finding: all rollouts note F is Hermitian with real eigenvalues by the spectral theorem; the question states F is Hermitian with a known spectrum.
provenance.discriminates: A response that treats eigenvalues of F as potentially complex, losing the phase property of det U.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Real added depth; gold=FAIL and 0/2, minimal weight.

validation.gold_why: Does not explicitly state F's eigenvalues are real.

items.title: Correct scalar c
items.description: The response gives c = e^{-iα/N} (or equivalently c = (det U)^{-1/N}), where N is the rank or dimension of the matrix, and connects this to the fact that α is real so the Nth root always exists.

provenance.evidence_detail: The mined pitfall 'Incomplete existence proof' flags responses that give the formula without justifying that the root always exists.
provenance.discriminates: A response that states c = (det U)^{-1/N} without linking it to the phase form det U = e^{iα}.
provenance.calibration_rationale: 1.00 discrimination, caught 2/2; central to the existence proof.

validation.gold_why: Does not explicitly connect c existence to α being real.

items.title: Nth-power determinant rule
items.description: The response uses the scalar-multiplication rule det(cU) = c^N det(U), where N is the matrix dimension, and avoids writing det(cU) = c det(U).

provenance.evidence_detail: The mined pitfall 'Missing dimension factor in det(cU)' flags the common mistake of writing det(cU) = c·det(U).
provenance.discriminates: A response that writes det(cU) = c det(U) instead of c^N det(U), leading to a wrong c.
provenance.calibration_rationale: 0.50 discrimination, caught 1/2; load-bearing intermediate for the unimodular proof.

validation.gold_why: Does not explicitly use det(cU)=c^N det(U).

items.title: Explicit det U' verification
items.description: The response explicitly shows that det(U') = c^N det(U) = e^{-iα}·e^{iα} = 1, confirming the unimodular result.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (c) demands a proof that det(U') = 1; the reference states 'we indeed have det U' = 1'.
provenance.discriminates: A response that asserts the result without showing the cancellation c^N · det(U) = 1.
provenance.calibration_rationale: 1.00 discrimination, caught 2/2; the explicit verification requested by the question.

validation.gold_why: Says det U'=1 but does not show the steps explicitly.

items.title: Unitarity of U' preserved
items.description: The response notes that |c| = 1 since c = e^{-iα/N} is a pure phase, so the transformed matrix U' = cU remains unitary.

provenance.evidence_detail: The mined pitfall 'Not preserving unitarity of U'' notes that |c| = 1 should be verified to keep U' unitary.
provenance.discriminates: A response that chooses a non-unit-modulus c without acknowledging the unitarity constraint.
provenance.calibration_rationale: 0.50 discrimination, caught 1/2; real added depth about unitarity preservation.

validation.gold_why: Does not note |c|=1 or that U' remains unitary.

items.title: Avoids wrong phase sign
items.description: Avoids using c = exp(+iα/N) instead of exp(-iα/N), which would double the phase rather than cancel it.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Sign error in exponent phase', severity high: using +iα/N gives det(U') = e^{2iα} ≠ 1.
provenance.discriminates: A response that picks the wrong sign in the exponent of c.
provenance.calibration_rationale: 0.50 discrimination, caught 1/2; specific sign error observed in flawed responses.

validation.gold_why: Uses negative exponent e^{-iα/N}, correct sign.

items.title: Avoids det U = 1 overclaim
items.description: Avoids stating that det U = 1 for a general unitary matrix, instead of |det U| = 1 or det U = e^{iα}.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference explicitly shows det U = e^{iα}, not 1; a response that claims det U = 1 for all unitary matrices contradicts the reference.
provenance.discriminates: A response that overstates the result by dropping the phase freedom of the determinant.
provenance.calibration_rationale: 0/2 discrimination but covers a common conceptual overclaim specific to this question.

validation.gold_why: Does not claim det U = 1 for general unitary.

items.title: Avoids wrong det(exp) identity
items.description: Avoids writing det(exp(iF)) = exp(det(iF)) or det(exp(iF)) = Tr(exp(iF)) instead of exp(i Tr F).

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Wrong identity for det(exp(A))', severity high: confuses the standard identity with other trace-determinant relations.
provenance.discriminates: A response that applies a muddled formula for the determinant of a matrix exponential.
provenance.calibration_rationale: 0/2 discrimination but names a specific incorrect identity for the matrix-exponential determinant.
provenance.merged_mirror_text: Avoids writing det U = ∏_k λ_k (the product of eigenvalues of F) instead of ∏_k e^{iλ_k} = exp(i Σ_k λ_k).

validation.gold_why: Uses exp(i Tr F), correct identity.

items.title: Existence from real phase
items.description: The response connects the existence of the transform U' = cU to the established fact that det U = e^{iα} with α real, so c = e^{-iα/N} is always well-defined.

provenance.evidence_detail: The mined pitfall 'Incomplete existence proof' flags responses that give the formula without justifying that the root always exists.
provenance.discriminates: A response that states c = (det U)^{-1/N} without linking it to the phase form det U = e^{iα}.
provenance.calibration_rationale: 1.00 discrimination, caught 2/2; ties the proof together by grounding existence in the real phase.

validation.gold_why: Does not explicitly connect c existence to α being real.

items.title: Empirical meaning of relativity
items.description: States that the empirical meaning of relativity is operational — special relativity concerns observable instrument readings such as rods, clocks, and detectors, and no local experiment detects absolute uniform motion.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (a) asks for a discussion of the empirical meaning of relativity; consensus among all rollouts was that SR is operational, not metaphysical.
provenance.discriminates: A response that gives a purely philosophical or metaphysical account of relativity without grounding it in observable quantities.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Core to the question but 0/2 discrimination and gold=FAIL; kept at Important for centrality.

validation.gold_why: Not stated in reference answer.

items.title: Spacetime interval invariance
items.description: States that the spacetime interval ds² = c²dt² − dx² − dy² − dz² is invariant under Lorentz transformations across different inertial frames.

provenance.evidence_detail: All three rollouts agreed that spacetime interval invariance is a core SR principle.
provenance.discriminates: A response that discusses Lorentz transformations but never identifies the invariant quantity or gets its sign signature wrong.
provenance.calibration_rationale: 1/2 discrimination; load-bearing SR formula anchoring frame-independence.

validation.gold_why: Not stated in reference answer.

items.title: Operational SR tests
items.description: Describes at least one operational test of special relativity across different inertial frames, such as time dilation (Δt = γΔτ), length contraction (L = L₀/γ), or relativity of simultaneity (Δt′ = −γvΔx/c²).

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (b) explicitly asks how SR principles can be operationally tested when measuring events in different inertial frames.
provenance.discriminates: A response that names SR phenomena but never ties them to measurable procedures or correct transformation formulas.
provenance.calibration_rationale: 0/2 discrimination but directly covers the 'operationally tested' sub-question.

validation.gold_why: No operational test described.

items.title: Position-momentum uncertainty
items.description: States that the Heisenberg uncertainty principle ΔxΔp ≥ ℏ/2 limits the spatial precision with which events can be localized in quantum mechanics, posing challenges to operational measurement in relativity.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (c) asks to address challenges posed by the uncertainty principle; all rollouts identified ΔxΔp ≥ ℏ/2 as limiting spatial localization.
provenance.discriminates: A response that mentions the uncertainty principle generically without specifying how it bounds event localization.
provenance.calibration_rationale: 0/2 discrimination but addresses the uncertainty principle sub-question directly.

validation.gold_why: Only generic measurement limitations mentioned.

items.title: Energy-time uncertainty
items.description: States that the energy-time uncertainty relation ΔEΔt ≥ ℏ/2 limits the temporal resolution of event measurement in quantum mechanics.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts identified ΔEΔt ≥ ℏ/2 as limiting temporal resolution of event measurement.
provenance.discriminates: A response that discusses spatial uncertainty only and ignores the temporal limitation on testing simultaneity or clock synchronization.
provenance.calibration_rationale: 2/2 discrimination; directly links measurement limitations to temporal event resolution.

validation.gold_why: Not stated in reference answer.

items.title: Avoids circular Δt notation
items.description: Avoids writing the energy-time uncertainty relation as ΔEΔt ~ ℏ/Δt (using Δt self-referentially on both sides) or treating Δt as a standard deviation of a self-adjoint time operator with the same status as position-momentum uncertainty.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Circular Δt notation' (medium severity) observed in rollout 1's declared final answer.
provenance.discriminates: A response that writes a dimensionally and logically inconsistent ΔEΔt expression from one that uses the correct form.
provenance.calibration_rationale: 1/2 discrimination; absorbed item 8 which added 0/2 but same conceptual error.

validation.gold_why: No circular Δt notation present.

items.title: Statistics connects QM and SR
items.description: States that statistics connects the limitations of measurement in quantum mechanics to the operational testing of special relativity across different inertial frames.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference answer emphasizes 'the role of statistics' as the unifying framework, whereas all rollouts treated statistics as one topic among several rather than the central connecting theme.
provenance.discriminates: A response that mentions probabilistic outcomes as a sub-topic rather than as the load-bearing bridge between QM measurement and SR covariance.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Gold=pass, 1/2 discrimination; central thesis linking QM measurement to SR tests.

validation.gold_why: Statistics linked to QM measurement and SR interaction.

items.title: Ensembles required
items.description: States that single quantum measurement outcomes are probabilistic and that operational tests of special relativity therefore require statistical ensembles rather than individual deterministic events.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts agreed that QM measurement is probabilistic and requires statistical ensembles for SR verification.
provenance.discriminates: A response that describes SR tests as if single quantum events (one decay, one detection) can verify Lorentz transformations.
provenance.calibration_rationale: 1/2 discrimination; key reasoning for why SR tests differ in QM versus classical physics.

validation.gold_why: Ensembles not explicitly mentioned.

items.title: Lorentz covariance of distributions
items.description: States that special relativity is tested in quantum mechanics by verifying the Lorentz covariance of probability distributions — such as cross-sections, decay rates, or spectra — across different inertial frames, not by individual deterministic events.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts agreed that SR in QM is tested via covariance of probability distributions across frames.
provenance.discriminates: A response that frames SR verification in terms of single-particle trajectory measurements without invoking distribution-level covariance.
provenance.calibration_rationale: 1/2 discrimination; specifies the concrete observable tested, complementing item 8.

validation.gold_why: Not stated in reference answer.

items.title: Microcausality and no-signaling
items.description: States that spacelike-separated local observables commute, [O(x), O(y)] = 0 for (x−y)² < 0, ensuring no-signaling and Lorentz-covariant probability distributions in quantum mechanics.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts agreed that no-signaling/microcausality ensures SR compatibility.
provenance.discriminates: A response that raises the challenge of frame-dependent measurement but never states the mechanism preserving Lorentz covariance.
provenance.calibration_rationale: 2/2 discrimination; formal principle ensuring QM consistency with SR.

validation.gold_why: Not stated in reference answer.

items.title: Avoids collapse violating Lorentz
items.description: Avoids asserting or implying that wavefunction collapse is a physical process in a preferred frame that violates the principles of relativity or enables superluminal signaling between different inertial frames.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Collapse violates Lorentz' (high severity, foreseen) about claiming QM is incompatible with SR.
provenance.discriminates: A response that concludes QM measurement is fundamentally incompatible with SR from one that correctly treats collapse as a non-relativistic bookkeeping tool.
provenance.calibration_rationale: 0/2 discrimination; real conceptual trap but no observed failures in test set.

validation.gold_why: No collapse-violating-Lorentz assertion present.

items.title: Compton wavelength limit
items.description: States that below the Compton wavelength λ_C = ℏ/(mc), localization energy creates particle-antiparticle pairs, requiring quantum field theory rather than single-particle position operators.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts identified the Compton wavelength as the boundary where the single-particle picture breaks down.
provenance.discriminates: A response that asserts event positions can be localized to arbitrary precision in principle with only ΔxΔp as a bound.
provenance.calibration_rationale: 2/2 discrimination; concrete limit on localization relevant to event measurement.

validation.gold_why: Not stated in reference answer.

items.title: Avoids classical SR only
items.description: Avoids presenting special relativity as only Lorentz transformations, time dilation, and length contraction without connecting them to the role of measurement, uncertainty, and statistics in quantum mechanics.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Classical SR only, QM grafted on' (high severity, reference_contrast) about not genuinely addressing QM measurement limits within SR operational tests.
provenance.discriminates: A response that treats SR classically throughout and mentions the uncertainty principle only in a disconnected final paragraph.
provenance.calibration_rationale: 1/2 discrimination; guards against omitting the QM-measurement aspect entirely.

validation.gold_why: SR connected to QM measurement and uncertainty.

items.title: Energy-momentum as SR test
items.description: States that the relativistic energy-momentum relation E² = p²c² + m²c⁴ and its Lorentz transformation (E′ = γ(E − vp_x), p′x = γ(p_x − vE/c²)) are predictions of special relativity that can be tested in different inertial frames.

provenance.evidence_detail: Rollout 2 explicitly included the energy-momentum relation as an operational test; rollouts 1 and 3 did not; the reference is silent.
provenance.discriminates: A response that includes four-momentum covariance as an additional SR test from one that covers only spacetime coordinate transformations.
provenance.calibration_rationale: 2/2 discrimination; additional concrete SR prediction testable across frames.

validation.gold_why: Not stated in reference answer.

items.title: Photon position operator
items.description: States that photons lack an exact position operator in quantum mechanics, complicating the localization of events involving photons in operational tests of relativity.

provenance.evidence_detail: Rollout 2 explicitly stated photons lack an exact position operator; rollouts 1 and 3 did not; the reference is silent.
provenance.discriminates: A response that acknowledges the photon localization problem from one that assumes all particles including photons have well-defined position operators.
provenance.calibration_rationale: 2/2 discrimination; genuine added depth on measurement limitations for massless particles.

validation.gold_why: Not stated in reference answer.

items.title: Explicit potential formula
items.description: Provides an explicit mathematical function for V(x1-x2) as the example potential, such as a Gaussian like V0 exp(-α(x1-x2)²) or a soft-core Coulomb form -1/√(x²+ε²).

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference answer names the Gaussian Effective Potential and the soft-core Coulomb potential; no rollout used either.
provenance.discriminates: A response that uses only a cosine-based example and never references the two named potentials from the reference.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Gold passed; discrimination 0.67 from naming examples. Core deliverable of the question.

validation.gold_why: Names Gaussian and soft-core Coulomb potentials explicitly.

items.title: Globally smooth stated
items.description: States the example potential is globally smooth with no singularities or branch points.

provenance.evidence_detail: The question's given constraint is that V is globally smooth; sub-question (b) targets properties including smoothness.
provenance.discriminates: A response that proposes a potential without verifying it is globally smooth and free of singularities or branch points.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Gold passed; directly answers the smoothness sub-question. Foundational requirement.

validation.gold_why: States globally smooth, no singularities or branch points.

items.title: Suitable for modeling
items.description: States the potential is suitable for modeling fermionic interactions because it does not introduce singularities.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference answer states these potentials are suitable for modeling fermionic interactions as they do not introduce singularities or branch points.
provenance.discriminates: A response that gives a formula but never states its suitability for modeling fermionic interactions.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Gold passed; discrimination 0.67. Connects smoothness to fermionic interaction modeling.

validation.gold_why: States suitability for modeling due to no singularities.

items.title: Periodicity on circle
items.description: States the potential is periodic on the circle V(s+L)=V(s) or uses an angular coordinate.

provenance.evidence_detail: High-severity mined pitfall 'Non-periodic on circle': proposing a potential smooth on ℝ but not well-defined on S¹.
provenance.discriminates: A response that writes a bare soft-core Coulomb or unperiodized Gaussian and never addresses the circle topology.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Gold FAIL but caught 1/3 negatives. Periodicity is the key circle-topology constraint.

validation.gold_why: Periodicity on the circle is never mentioned.

items.title: Exchange symmetry
items.description: States the potential is exchange-symmetric, V(-s)=V(s), for two identical fermionic particles.

provenance.evidence_detail: High-severity mined pitfall 'Exchange symmetry dropped': proposing V(s) with V(-s)≠V(s) for identical fermions.
provenance.discriminates: A response that proposes an asymmetric potential such as exp(-α(x1-x2)) without an absolute value or squared argument.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Gold FAIL, caught 0/3. Essential physics: identical-particle symmetry of V.

validation.gold_why: Exchange symmetry V(-s)=V(s) is not discussed.

items.title: Pauli from antisymmetry
items.description: States the Pauli exclusion principle arises from the antisymmetry of the fermionic wavefunction, not from the smoothness or finiteness of V(x1-x2).

provenance.evidence_detail: High-severity mined pitfall 'Potential causes Pauli': asserting that smoothness or finiteness of V is what enforces Pauli exclusion.
provenance.discriminates: A response that claims the smooth potential at x1-x2=0 'implements' or 'ensures' the Pauli exclusion principle.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Gold split; conceptual crux of the question. Avoids the common V-causes-Pauli error.

validation.gold_why: Does not discuss antisymmetry of wavefunction as Pauli origin.

items.title: Finite at coincidence
items.description: States the potential is bounded and finite at coincidence x1-x2=0.

provenance.evidence_detail: All three rollouts agree the potential is bounded and finite at x1=x2; this is a required property for sub-question (b).
provenance.discriminates: A response whose example potential diverges or is undefined at x1-x2=0.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Gold FAIL, caught 0/3. Concrete property distinguishing smooth from singular potentials.

validation.gold_why: Finiteness at coincidence is not explicitly stated.

items.title: No singular forces
items.description: States the smoothness of the potential leads to no singular forces or divergences in the Schrödinger equation.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (c) asks how smoothness affects the behavior of the system; consensus across rollouts is that smoothness removes singular forces and boundary conditions.
provenance.discriminates: A response that discusses Pauli exclusion but never connects the smoothness of V to the regularity of the dynamics.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Gold FAIL, caught 0/3. Connects smoothness to well-defined dynamics.

validation.gold_why: No mention of singular forces or Schrödinger equation divergences.

items.title: Node for same-spin
items.description: States that for same-spin fermionic particles the spatial wavefunction vanishes at coincidence ψ(x,x)=0 independent of the potential V(x1-x2).

provenance.evidence_detail: All three rollouts agree ψ(x,x)=0 for same-spin fermions is statistical, not caused by V; this is load-bearing for sub-question (c).
provenance.discriminates: A response that either claims the node comes from V or never mentions that same-spin fermions cannot coincide.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Gold FAIL, caught 1/3 negatives. Key Pauli-principle physics independent of V.

validation.gold_why: Node at coincidence for same-spin fermions not mentioned.

items.title: Opposite-spin coincidence
items.description: States that opposite-spin fermionic particles in a spin singlet can coincide at x1-x2=0 and feel finite V(0) without a node in the spatial wavefunction.

items.title: Diene HOMO to dienophile LUMO
