validation.gold_why: Shows sin cos integral vanishes, yielding ⟨p_x⟩ = 0.

items.title: Probability integral setup
items.description: The response sets up the probability for part (b) as the integral of |ψ_n|² = (2/a) sin²(nπx/a) over the range a/3 to 2a/3, including the 2/a normalization prefactor.

provenance.evidence_detail: Pitfall 'Dropping normalization factor': forgetting the 2/a from the eigenfunction normalization.
provenance.discriminates: A response whose probability values are too large by a factor of 2.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Standard setup; absorbed normalization pitfall and limits into one checkable item.

validation.gold_why: Includes the 2/a prefactor in all probability integrals.

items.title: Probability density as integral
items.description: The response defines the probability in part (b) as the integral of the probability density |ψ_n(x)|² over the specified range a/3 to 2a/3, not as a single-point evaluation.

provenance.evidence_detail: The question asks for probability in a range; the reference computes ∫ψ²dx over the interval.
provenance.discriminates: A response that evaluates |ψ|² at a single point instead of integrating over the range.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Conceptual anchor for the integration; low discrimination but guards a common misunderstanding.

validation.gold_why: Defines probability as integral of |ψ_n|² over the range.

items.title: Ground state probability
items.description: The response gives the ground state (n=1) probability in the range a/3 to 2a/3 as approximately 0.609 (or equivalently 1/3 + √3/(2π)).

provenance.evidence_detail: Part (b) target: P_ground; reference and all rollouts agree on 0.609.
provenance.discriminates: A response that gives 0.058 or any other value for the ground state probability.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 1/2 negatives; this is one of the three explicitly requested numerical results.

validation.gold_why: Gives ground state probability as 0.609.

items.title: First excited probability
items.description: The response gives the first excited state (n=2) probability in the range a/3 to 2a/3 as approximately 0.196 (or equivalently 1/3 − √3/(4π)).

provenance.evidence_detail: Part (b) target: P_first excited; reference and all rollouts agree on 0.196.
provenance.discriminates: A response that gives 0.609 or 0.333 for the first excited state probability.
provenance.calibration_rationale: One of three requested numerical results; essential for completeness of part (b).

validation.gold_why: Gives first excited state probability as 0.196.

items.title: Second excited probability
items.description: The response gives the second excited state (n=3) probability in the range a/3 to 2a/3 as approximately 0.333 or exactly 1/3, noting that the sine correction terms cancel exactly.

provenance.evidence_detail: Part (b) target: P_second excited; reference states 0.333.
provenance.discriminates: A response that gives 0.196 or 0.609 for the second excited state probability.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Third requested numerical result; the exact 1/3 cancellation is a meaningful intermediate.

validation.gold_why: Gives second excited state probability as 0.333.

items.title: Avoids wrong sin(4π/3) sign
items.description: Avoids evaluating sin(4π/3) as +√3/2 when computing the ground state probability; the response uses sin(4π/3) = −√3/2.

provenance.evidence_detail: Pitfall 'Sign of sin(4π/3)': evaluating sin(4π/3) as positive leads to P₁ ≈ 0.058 instead of 0.609.
provenance.discriminates: A response that reaches 0.058 for the ground state due to a sign error on sin(4π/3).
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 1/2 negatives; sign error in this specific sine value flips the ground-state result.

validation.gold_why: Uses sin(4π/3) = −√3/2 implicitly; gets +0.866/π correction.

items.title: Avoids wrong sin(8π/3) value
items.description: Avoids evaluating sin(8π/3) as −√3/2; the response correctly evaluates sin(8π/3) = √3/2 when computing the first excited state probability.

provenance.evidence_detail: Pitfall 'sin(8π/3) periodicity error': mishandling the reduction of 8π/3 leads to wrong P₂.
provenance.discriminates: A response that evaluates sin(8π/3) incorrectly and gets the wrong value for P₂.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Zero measured discrimination but names a specific periodicity trap for the n=2 calculation.

validation.gold_why: Evaluates sin(8π/3) = √3/2 correctly; result 0.196 confirms this.

items.title: Product-to-sum identity
items.description: The response uses the identity sin²(nπx/a) = (1/2)(1 − cos(2nπx/a)) to convert the probability integral into a cosine integral.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference answer writes the integral as (1/a)∫(1 − cos(2nπx/a))dx for each state.
provenance.discriminates: A response that attempts direct integration of sin² without using the power-reduction identity and gets stuck.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Load-bearing intermediate step that all three probability evaluations depend on.

validation.gold_why: Uses sin² = (1/2)(1 − cos(2nπx/a)) identity via 1 − cos form.

items.title: Three probabilities provided
items.description: The response provides explicit numerical or closed-form probability values for all three states: ground state, first excited state, and second excited state.

provenance.evidence_detail: Part (b) requires probabilities for ground, first excited, and second excited states.
provenance.discriminates: A response that gives only one or two of the three required probabilities.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Directly addresses the completeness of part (b); ensures all three requested results are present.

validation.gold_why: Provides values for all three states: 0.609, 0.196, 0.333.

items.title: Standing wave interpretation
items.description: The response interprets the n=1 state of the particle in a box as a standing wave composed of equal leftward and rightward travelling components, explaining the zero average momentum.

provenance.evidence_detail: Consensus correct claim: average momentum is zero because the real stationary-state eigenfunction decomposes into equal +p and −p components.
provenance.discriminates: A response that attributes the zero to a mathematical accident rather than the standing-wave structure.

validation.gold_why: Does not mention standing wave or travelling wave components.

validation_summary.pitfall_weight_convention: stored on the RaR -1/-2 scale by schema.Criterion; graded by magnitude with polarity=positive

items.title: Three-partition more microstates
items.description: States that the configuration with the box divided into three equal parts, each containing one-third of the molecules, has more microstates than the two-part configuration, and also states how this relates to entropy.

provenance.evidence_detail: All three rollouts concluded Ω₁ = Ω₂, contradicting the reference which states the three-partition configuration has more microstates.
provenance.discriminates: A response that concludes both configurations have equal microstates.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 3/3 negatives; directly answers the core question about which configuration has more microstates.

validation.gold_why: Does not state three-partition has more microstates.

items.title: Combinatorial multiplicity formula
items.description: Uses the combinatorial assignment multiplicity W = N!/(∏N_i!) as the basis for counting microstates of each configuration of the ideal gas, rather than the full per-compartment indistinguishable-particle phase-space volume.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts used per-compartment phase-space volumes ∏[V_i^{N_i}/N_i!] which collapsed to identical entropies, whereas the reference's intended comparison uses W = N!/∏N_i!.
provenance.discriminates: A response that replaces the combinatorial multiplicity with the full Gibbs-corrected phase-space volume, causing the comparison to vanish.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 3/3 negatives; the wrong formula choice leads to the equal-microstates error.

validation.gold_why: No formula used in the answer.

items.title: Two-compartment W expression
items.description: Writes the explicit combinatorial multiplicity for the box divided into two equal parts as W₂ = N! / [(N/2)!]² or equivalent, with N = 1 mole of molecules.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (c) requires explicit derivation of Ω for each configuration; W₂ = N!/[(N/2)!]² is the load-bearing intermediate expression.
provenance.discriminates: A response that jumps to ln W₂ = N ln 2 without showing the factorial expression.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 3/3 negatives; required intermediate expression for the two-compartment calculation.

validation.gold_why: W₂ expression not shown.

items.title: Three-compartment W expression
items.description: Writes the explicit combinatorial multiplicity for the box divided into three equal parts as W₃ = N! / [(N/3)!]³ or equivalent, with N = 1 mole of molecules.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (c) requires explicit derivation; W₃ = N!/[(N/3)!]³ is the load-bearing intermediate expression.
provenance.discriminates: A response that jumps to ln W₃ = N ln 3 without showing the factorial expression.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 3/3 negatives; required intermediate expression for the three-compartment calculation.

validation.gold_why: W₃ expression not shown.

items.title: ln W₂ approx N ln 2
items.description: Derives or states ln W₂ ≈ N ln 2 for the two-compartment configuration by applying Stirling's approximation to W = N! / [(N/2)!]².

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (c) requires explicit derivation of Ω for each configuration; the combinatorial multiplicity for the box divided into two equal parts gives ln W₂ = N ln 2.
provenance.discriminates: A response that does not provide the explicit ln W₂ value or derives it incorrectly.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 3/3 negatives; key intermediate result in comparing the two configurations of molecules.

validation.gold_why: No derivation of ln W₂.

items.title: ln W₃ approx N ln 3
items.description: Derives or states ln W₃ ≈ N ln 3 for the three-compartment configuration by applying Stirling's approximation to W = N! / [(N/3)!]³.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (c) requires explicit derivation of Ω for each configuration; the combinatorial multiplicity for the box divided into three equal parts gives ln W₃ = N ln 3.
provenance.discriminates: A response that does not provide the explicit ln W₃ value or derives it incorrectly.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 3/3 negatives; key intermediate result showing three compartments yield more microstates.

validation.gold_why: No derivation of ln W₃.

items.title: Ratio W₃/W₂ quantified
items.description: Quantifies the ratio W₃/W₂ = (3/2)^N or equivalently ln(W₃/W₂) = N ln(3/2) for comparing the microstates of the three-part versus two-part configuration.

provenance.evidence_detail: The 'Ratio unquantified' pitfall notes that many responses state 'more' qualitatively but never compute W₃/W₂ = (3/2)^N or its log.
provenance.discriminates: A response that claims three compartments have more microstates but never quantifies the ratio.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 3/3 negatives; the direct quantitative comparison of microstates between configurations.

validation.gold_why: Ratio not quantified.

items.title: Boltzmann relation applied
items.description: Connects the microstate count to entropy using the Boltzmann relation S = k_B ln Ω for both configurations of the ideal gas system.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (b) explicitly asks how the microstate count relates to the entropy of the system; the implicit constraints specify S = k_B ln Ω.
provenance.discriminates: A response that gives the microstate comparison but never invokes S = k_B ln Ω.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 1/3 negatives; required to relate microstates to entropy as the question asks.

validation.gold_why: Boltzmann relation not mentioned.

items.title: S₃ greater than S₂
items.description: States that the entropy of the three-compartment configuration is greater than the entropy of the two-compartment configuration because W₃ > W₂ and S = k_B ln Ω is monotonically increasing in Ω.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts concluded ΔS = 0; the reference implies S₃ > S₂ since the three-partition has more microstates.
provenance.discriminates: A response that concludes the entropies are equal.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 3/3 negatives; directly answers the entropy sub-question linking microstates to the system.

validation.gold_why: Entropy comparison not stated.

items.title: Entropy difference computed
items.description: Computes the entropy difference ΔS = S₃ − S₂ = k_B N ln(3/2) = R ln(3/2) ≈ +3.4 J/K for 1 mole of molecules.

provenance.evidence_detail: The 'Ratio unquantified' pitfall's correct result specifies ΔS_combinatorial = k_B ln(W₃/W₂) = R ln(3/2) > 0.
provenance.discriminates: A response that states S₃ > S₂ but never computes the numerical entropy difference.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 3/3 negatives; the requested detailed calculation of the entropy difference.

validation.gold_why: Entropy difference not computed.

items.title: Stirling approximation justified
items.description: Applies Stirling's approximation ln(n!) ≈ n ln n − n to the factorials in the combinatorial multiplicity, justified because N = 1 mole ≈ 6×10²³ molecules.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (c) demands a detailed calculation; the implicit constraints state Stirling's approximation is justified for N ~ 10²³.
provenance.discriminates: A response that attempts exact factorial arithmetic or does not invoke Stirling's approximation.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 1/3 negatives; load-bearing methodological step in the detailed calculation.

validation.gold_why: Stirling approximation not applied.

items.title: Avogadro's number used
items.description: Uses N = N_A (Avogadro's number) for the 1 mole of molecules so that N k_B = R when computing the entropy of the system.

provenance.evidence_detail: The question specifies 1 mole of an ideal gas; the correct ΔS = R ln(3/2) requires using N = N_A.
provenance.discriminates: A response that treats N as an unspecified symbol without connecting it to the given 1 mole.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 0/3 negatives; genuinely necessary for the numerical entropy calculation but implied by context.

validation.gold_why: Avogadro's number not used.

items.title: Equal density noted
items.description: Notes that each compartment has the same number density N/V in both the two-part and three-part configurations, since each compartment of volume V/k contains N/k molecules.

provenance.evidence_detail: The implicit constraints state density = N/V regardless of k; the difficulty notes highlight this as the crucial subtlety.
provenance.discriminates: A response that incorrectly claims the densities differ between configurations.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 1/3 negatives; real physical insight distinguishing configurational from density effects.

validation.gold_why: Density argument not noted.

items.title: Avoids entropy-multiplicity conflation
items.description: Avoids equating the extensive thermodynamic configurational entropy of uniform-density sub-volumes with the combinatorial macrostate multiplicity W = N!/∏N_i! that the question asks to compare.

provenance.evidence_detail: The 'Entropy vs multiplicity' pitfall: responses identified the same extensive S and reported equality of microstates.
provenance.discriminates: A response that argues no entropy change implies same number of microstates.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 3/3 negatives; specific wrong move where flawed responses conflated entropy with multiplicity.

validation.gold_why: Does not conflate entropy with multiplicity.

items.title: Avoids double Gibbs correction
items.description: Avoids applying the 1/N! indistinguishability correction both globally on the total N and per compartment on each N_i when computing the combinatorial multiplicity W = N!/∏N_i! for 1 mole of molecules in the box.

provenance.evidence_detail: The 'Double Gibbs factor' pitfall: applying 1/N! on top of 1/N_i! per compartment introduces a spurious factor that can flip the comparison.
provenance.discriminates: A response that double-counts the Gibbs correction and gets a ratio dependent on 1/N!.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 1/3 negatives; subtle overcounting error but less frequently observed in flawed responses.

validation.gold_why: Does not apply double Gibbs correction.

validation_summary.pitfall_weight_convention: stored on the RaR -1/-2 scale by schema.Criterion; graded by magnitude with polarity=positive

items.title: WPL gene order
items.description: States the gene sequence for W, P, and L as WPL (or L–P–W) with P located in the middle.

provenance.evidence_detail: Part (a) requires concluding the order of W, P, L; reference states 'the gene sequence is WPL.'
provenance.discriminates: A response that gives a wrong order such as W–L–P or fails to commit to an order.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Core answer to sub-question 1; disc 0.00 but correctness collapses without it.

validation.gold_why: States gene sequence is WPL with P in middle.

items.title: ABC gene order
items.description: States the gene sequence for A, B, and C as ABC (or C–B–A) with B in the middle.

provenance.evidence_detail: Part (b) asks about relative position of A, B, C; reference states 'the sequence is ABC.'
provenance.discriminates: A response that says the ABC order cannot be determined or leaves part (b) without a committed order.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Core answer to sub-question 2; disc 0.00 but correctness collapses without it.

validation.gold_why: States the sequence is ABC with B in middle.

items.title: W-L flanking genes
items.description: Identifies W and L as the flanking (outer) genes because W and L are never cotransduced.

provenance.evidence_detail: Reference concludes W–L are not cotransduced so they exceed the packaging limit and must be the outer pair.
provenance.discriminates: A response that places W and L adjacent or fails to use their non-cotransduction to identify them as outer.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Key reasoning for WPL order; disc 0.00 so low weight despite conceptual importance.
provenance.merged_mirror_text: Identifies A and C as the flanking (outer) genes because A and C are only infrequently cotransduced.

validation.gold_why: W and L not cotransduced, flanking P in WPL order.

items.title: ABC order definitive
items.description: Concludes the ABC order as a definitive result rather than hedging it as tentative or less certain.

provenance.evidence_detail: Rollout 3 hedged the ABC inference as 'less certain'; reference treats ABC as definitive with a mechanistic explanation.
provenance.discriminates: A response that correctly states ABC but adds a caveat that the inference is weaker or less certain than the WPL conclusion.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Disc 1.00; absorbed avoidance of declaring ABC indeterminate, which is a proven trap.

validation.gold_why: States 'the sequence is ABC' definitively.

items.title: 2% packaging limit
items.description: States that the transducing phage can carry only about 2 percent of the E. coli genome.

provenance.evidence_detail: Reference cites 'only about 2 percent of the E. coli genome can fit into a transducing phage'; no rollout included this value.
provenance.discriminates: A response that gives correct orders but never cites the physical packaging limit that grounds the reasoning.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Disc 0.50; specific numeric anchor central to both sub-questions' reasoning.

validation.gold_why: States about 2 percent of E. coli genome fits in phage.

items.title: W-L exceeds 2%
items.description: States that the W–L distance exceeds the 2 percent limit of the chromosome segment a phage can carry.

provenance.evidence_detail: Reference states 'the segment of chromosome that carries both W and L must exceed the 2 percent limit.'
provenance.discriminates: A response that says W–L are far apart but does not connect their non-cotransduction to exceeding the packaging limit.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Disc 1.00; load-bearing intermediate for WPL conclusion.

validation.gold_why: States W-L segment must exceed the 2 percent limit.

items.title: A-C within 2%
items.description: States that the A–C distance is close to but within the 2 percent limit.

provenance.evidence_detail: Reference states 'the A—C distance is less than that of the W—L region and is close to the 2 percent limit.'
provenance.discriminates: A response that gives the ABC order but does not explain why A–C is infrequent rather than never cotransduced.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Disc 1.00; load-bearing intermediate for ABC conclusion and infrequency explanation.

validation.gold_why: States A-C distance is close to the 2 percent limit.

items.title: A-C less than W-L
items.description: States that the A–C distance is less than the W–L distance.

provenance.evidence_detail: Reference explicitly compares: 'the A—C distance is less than that of the W—L region.'
provenance.discriminates: A response that treats both parts as analogous without distinguishing the physical difference between 'never' and 'infrequently.'
provenance.calibration_rationale: Disc 1.00; comparative detail adding depth across the two sub-questions.

validation.gold_why: States A-C distance is less than W-L distance.

items.title: Break-position mechanism
items.description: Explains that infrequent A–C cotransduction requires chromosomal breaks immediately outside both A and C loci, which occurs rarely.

provenance.evidence_detail: Reference states 'the breaks in the chromosome would have to be immediately outside the two loci, and this can only be expected to occur rarely.'
provenance.discriminates: A response that explains infrequency only qualitatively as 'larger distance' without the break-position mechanism.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Disc 1.00; mechanistic explanation directly answering why A–C is infrequent.

validation.gold_why: Breaks must be immediately outside both loci, occurring rarely.

items.title: Genes >2% not cotransduced
items.description: States that genes separated by more than about 2 percent of the total chromosome will not be cotransduced.

provenance.evidence_detail: Reference states 'Genes that are separated by a length of DNA that comprises more than about 2 percent of the total chromosome will not be cotransduced.'
provenance.discriminates: A response that cites the 2% packaging limit but does not state its consequence for cotransduction.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Disc 1.00; general principle grounding both sub-questions.

validation.gold_why: States genes separated by more than 2 percent won't cotransduce.

items.title: W-P and P-L within 2%
items.description: States that W and P, and P and L, are close enough to be located on a piece of E. coli chromosome that is less than 2 percent of the total length.

provenance.evidence_detail: Reference states 'W and P, and P and L, can be cotransduced, so we conclude that they are close enough to be located on a piece of E. coli chromosome that is less than 2 percent.'
provenance.discriminates: A response that only discusses the non-cotransduced pair without applying the 2% limit to the cotransducible pairs.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Disc 1.00; applies packaging limit to the cotransduced pairs in sub-question 1.

validation.gold_why: States W-P and P-L are within 2 percent limit.

items.title: Phage carries small piece
items.description: States that the phage vector can carry only a small piece of donor chromosome to the cell about to be transduced.

provenance.evidence_detail: Reference opens with 'the phage vector can carry only a small piece of the donor chromosome to the cell about to be transduced.'
provenance.discriminates: A response that gives orders and the 2% value but never states the basic mechanism of transducing phage packaging.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Disc 0.50; background context without the specific 2 percent anchor already covered above.

validation.gold_why: States phage carries only a small piece of donor chromosome.

items.title: Closely linked cotransduce
items.description: States that only closely linked genes can be cotransduced.

provenance.evidence_detail: Reference states 'only genes that are closely linked can be cotransduced'; rollouts omitted this general framing.
provenance.discriminates: A response that jumps to specific orders without stating the general condition for cotransduction.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Disc 0.50; general principle, less specific than the 2 percent criteria already listed.

validation.gold_why: States only closely linked genes can be cotransduced.

items.title: Avoids reversing distance logic
items.description: Avoids reversing the distance–cotransduction relationship by claiming that easily cotransduced genes are far apart or that the non-cotransduced pair must be adjacent.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Reversed distance–cotransduction logic' (severity: high): foreseen error of flipping the inverse relationship.
provenance.discriminates: A response that places A and C adjacent because they are infrequently cotransduced, or places an easily cotransduced pair as the flanking pair.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Disc 0.00; specific bioinformatics trap, kept as low-weight Pitfall to flag the error.

validation.gold_why: Correctly treats easily cotransduced as close, non-cotransduced as far.

validation_summary.pitfall_weight_convention: stored on the RaR -1/-2 scale by schema.Criterion; graded by magnitude with polarity=positive

items.title: NPT Boltzmann weight
items.description: The response gives the isothermal-isobaric distribution as proportional to exp[−β(E + PV)] with the pressure-volume term inside the exponential adding to the energy, not subtracting from it.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (a) requires the derived NPT distribution; the reference formula p_{i,j} ∝ e^{-β[E_i(V_j) + PV_j]} fixes the functional form.
provenance.discriminates: A response that writes exp[-β(H - PV)] or exp[-βH] without the PV term.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Core result; gold=pass, caught 2/2 negatives, discrimination 1.00.

validation.gold_why: Answer gives exp[-β(E+PV)] with PV added inside exponential.

items.title: NPT partition function
items.description: The response writes the isothermal-isobaric partition function as Δ(N,P,T) = ∫₀^∞ dV e^{−βPV} Z(N,V,T), a Laplace transform of the canonical partition function over volume.

provenance.evidence_detail: All three consensus rollouts stated this relation; it is the standard integrated form of the NPT distribution.
provenance.discriminates: A response that omits the volume integral or writes a Fourier kernel e^{+iβPV} instead of the real decaying Laplace kernel.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 2/2 negatives; necessary for the derivation though gold=FAIL.

validation.gold_why: No partition function integral written.

items.title: Reservoir entropy derivation
items.description: The response derives the isothermal-isobaric distribution by expanding the reservoir entropy and using ∂S/∂E = 1/T and ∂S/∂V = +P/T, yielding ΔS_r = −(E + PV)/T.

provenance.evidence_detail: All three rollouts used this reservoir-entropy expansion as the derivation method.
provenance.discriminates: A response that uses ∂S/∂V = -P/T, which flips the sign of the PV term.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 2/2 negatives; load-bearing derivation step, gold=FAIL.

validation.gold_why: No reservoir entropy derivation given.

items.title: Extended phase space
items.description: The response introduces an extended phase space Γ_ext = Γ_{6N} × ℝ⁺ that supplements the classical 6N-dimensional phase space with volume as an additional coordinate conjugate to pressure.

provenance.evidence_detail: All three consensus rollouts constructed this extended phase space; it is the core of sub-question (b).
provenance.discriminates: A response that insists volume is strictly an external parameter that cannot appear as a coordinate on phase space.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Zero discrimination but necessary for sub-question (b) coverage.

validation.gold_why: No extended phase space mentioned.

items.title: Volume function on phase space
items.description: The response states that the Volume function is defined on the extended phase space as V(q, p, V) = V, making volume a dynamical function on phase space rather than merely a fixed boundary condition.

provenance.evidence_detail: All three rollouts defined this projection function on the extended phase space.
provenance.discriminates: A response that denies a Volume function can be defined on phase space at all.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 1/2 negatives; central to sub-question (b), gold=FAIL.

validation.gold_why: No Volume function on phase space discussed.

items.title: Hamiltonian volume dependence
items.description: The response states that the system Hamiltonian depends parametrically on the volume, written as H_N(q, p; V) or E_i(V_j), so that changing volume changes the energy levels of the system.

provenance.evidence_detail: All three rollouts used H_N(q,p;V) notation; the reference uses E_i(V_j).
provenance.discriminates: A response that treats the Hamiltonian as independent of the volume variable.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Gold=pass but zero discrimination; correct intermediate fact.

validation.gold_why: Answer writes E_i(V_j), showing volume dependence.

items.title: Quantum V as parameter
items.description: The response states that in standard quantum mechanics volume enters the Hamiltonian H(V) as a c-number parameter, not as an operator acting on the particle Hilbert space.

provenance.evidence_detail: All three consensus rollouts stated V is a parameter in H(V); this is the essential point of sub-question (c).
provenance.discriminates: A response that claims V̂ is already a standard operator on the particle Hilbert space without any extension.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 1/2 negatives; needed for sub-question (c) coverage.

validation.gold_why: No quantum mechanical treatment discussed.

items.title: Extended Hilbert space for V̂
items.description: The response explains that a true quantum volume-operator requires quantizing an added boundary degree of freedom on an extended Hilbert space, such as a direct integral over V or a tensor product with L²(ℝ⁺).

provenance.evidence_detail: Rollouts disagreed on whether the extended space is a direct integral or a tensor product, but all agreed some extension is needed for V̂.

items.title: States starting equation

items.title: Substitutes n = mass/molar mass

provenance.discriminates: A response that rearranges PV = nRT to n/V = P/(RT) and calls that 'density' without ever substituting n = mass/molar mass.

items.title: Writes substituted equation
items.description: Writes the substituted form of the equation as PV equals mass times RT divided by molar mass.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference writes PV = (w/m)RT as an explicit intermediate step; all rollouts produce an equivalent form.
provenance.discriminates: A response that substitutes n verbally but never writes the resulting equation.

items.title: Rearranges for mass/volume
items.description: Rearranges the equation to isolate mass divided by volume on one side.

provenance.discriminates: A response that substitutes n = m/M but leaves the equation in the form PV = (m/M)RT without isolating the density term.

items.title: Identifies mass/volume as density
items.description: Identifies mass per unit volume as density within the derivation.

items.title: Arrives at density expression

items.title: Molar mass is constant

items.title: Concludes density ∝ P

provenance.calibration_rationale: The requested final result; caught 1/2 negatives, answer is incomplete without it.

items.title: States proportionality conditions

provenance.discriminates: A response that states ρ ∝ P as a universal law without specifying it requires fixed temperature and a fixed gas identity.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Conditions make the result valid; caught 2/2 negatives via source 17, high discrimination.

items.title: Proportionality constant m/RT

provenance.discriminates: A response that states ρ ∝ P but never identifies what the proportionality constant is.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Explicit constant identification; caught 2/2 negatives, deep correctness signal.

validation.gold_why: m/RT is the proportionality constant in a = Pm/RT.

items.title: Avoids number density shortcut
items.description: Avoids presenting n/V as the density result without substituting n equal to mass divided by molar mass into the equation PV = nRT.

provenance.discriminates: A response that rearranges to n/V = P/(RT) and labels n/V as 'density' without ever introducing molar mass.

items.title: Initial separation
items.description: Writes the initial scalar separation of the two Brownian particles as $P_0 = |P_1 - P_2|$ using their starting coordinates $P_1$ and $P_2$.

provenance.discriminates: A response that does not define the initial separation or uses a different expression for $P_0$.

items.title: Relative displacement vector
items.description: Defines the relative displacement between the two Brownian particles as $R(t) = B_1(t) - B_2(t)$ in the three-dimensional fluid.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts define R(t) = B1(t) − B2(t) as the foundational step; this quantity is needed to derive the relative diffusion result.
provenance.discriminates: A response that computes results without defining the relative displacement vector.

items.title: Second moment formula
items.description: Presents the expression $\|P_0\|^2 + 2 \cdot (D_1 + D_2) \cdot t$ and identifies it as the second moment $E[|R(t)|^2]$ of the relative displacement magnitude after $t$ seconds.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts used coefficient 6 for the diffusion term in three dimensions, while the reference uses coefficient 2.
provenance.discriminates: A response that uses $\|P_0\|^2 + 6(D_1+D_2)t$ instead of the reference's coefficient 2.

items.title: Relative diffusion coefficient
items.description: States that the relative diffusion coefficient for the two Brownian particles is $D_1 + D_2$, given their respective diffusion coefficients $D_1$ and $D_2$.

provenance.discriminates: A response that introduces a reduced or modified effective coefficient instead of the simple sum.

items.title: D2=0 specialization
items.description: Explicitly specializes the change in distance expressions for the $D_2 = 0$ case, giving $\|P_0\|^2 + 2 \cdot D_1 \cdot t$ by replacing $D_1 + D_2$ with $D_1$.

provenance.discriminates: A response that gives a different D2=0 result, such as $\|P_0\|^2 + 6 D_1 t$ or does not write the reduced formula.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Source 5 caught 3/3 negatives; directly answers the second sub-question.

validation.gold_why: D2=0 case expression not provided.

items.title: B2 fixed when immobile
items.description: States that when $D_2 = 0$, particle $B_2$ remains fixed at its starting coordinates $P_2$ in the three-dimensional fluid.

provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 3/3 negatives; explains why the relative diffusion reduces to $D_1$.

items.title: Variance formula given
items.description: Provides an explicit formula for the variance of the change in distance between the two Brownian particles after $t$ seconds.

items.title: Mean subtracts initial separation

provenance.discriminates: A response that reports E[r(t)] as the mean change in distance without subtracting the initial separation $|P_1 - P_2|$.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 1/3 negatives; without subtracting $r_0$ the reported mean has the wrong offset.

validation.gold_why: Mean subtraction of initial separation not stated.

items.title: Variance not just second moment

provenance.discriminates: A response that presents $E[|R(t)|^2]$ alone as the variance without subtracting the squared mean.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 1/3 negatives; conflating variance with the second moment is a core conceptual error.

items.title: Convention for change in distance

provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 1/3 negatives; the convention determines which formulas apply.

provenance.discriminates: A response that treats the scalar distance as linearly Gaussian, ignoring the nonlinear |·| transformation.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 1/3 negatives; provides the distributional foundation for computing mean and variance.

validation.gold_why: Noncentral Maxwell distribution not identified.

items.title: Correct variable dependence
items.description: Presents expressions for the variance and mean of the change in distance that are functions of $D_1$, $D_2$, $|P_1 - P_2|$, and $t$ seconds.

provenance.discriminates: A response that gives expressions missing a dependence on one of D1, D2, the initial separation, or time.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 1/3 negatives; ensures the answer depends on all four relevant quantities.

items.title: Independent Brownian motions

provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 1/3 negatives; the vector short-cut gives a trivially zero mean and ignores the requested scalar distance.

validation.gold_why: Answer does not interpret change as vector with zero mean.

items.title: Quantum postulates start
items.description: The derivation begins from the fundamental postulates of quantum mechanics, specifically state vectors in Hilbert space, observables as Hermitian operators, and unitary time evolution, as the foundational starting point rather than classical phase-space concepts such as the Liouville theorem and ∫ d^{3N}p d^{3N}q.

provenance.evidence_detail: Pitfall 'Classical starting point' warns against using classical Hamiltonian flow as the foundation rather than quantum postulates.
provenance.discriminates: Catches responses that begin with classical Liouville mechanics and only later quantize.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Foundational starting point; 0/2 discrimination but genuinely necessary for the derivation.

items.title: Density operator bridge
items.description: The response introduces the density operator ρ = Σ_i p_i |ψ_i⟩⟨ψ_i| with Tr ρ = 1 as the bridge between quantum mechanics and statistical mechanics, giving ⟨A⟩ = Tr(ρA).

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts agreed on the density operator as the bridge from quantum to statistical mechanics, with the formula ρ = Σ_i p_i |ψ_i⟩⟨ψ_i|.
provenance.discriminates: Catches responses that discuss ensembles qualitatively without writing the density matrix formalism.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Core bridge concept; 0.50 discrimination, load-bearing for the entire derivation.

validation.gold_why: No density operator introduced.

items.title: Von Neumann Liouville equation
items.description: The response states the equation of motion for the density operator dρ/dt = -(i/ℏ)[H, ρ] in the derivation of the principles of statistical mechanics from quantum postulates.

provenance.evidence_detail: Rollouts agreed on dρ/dt = -(i/ℏ)[H,ρ] as the time evolution of the density operator.
provenance.discriminates: Catches responses that introduce ρ but omit its dynamical equation linking it to unitary quantum evolution.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Required equation of motion; 0.50 discrimination.

validation.gold_why: No equation of motion for density operator.

items.title: Microcanonical energy shell
items.description: The microcanonical ensemble is written as ρ_mc = (1/Ω(E)) Σ_{E_n ∈ [E, E+δE]} |n⟩⟨n|, restricting equal a priori probabilities to an energy shell rather than the full Hilbert space, in the derivation of statistical mechanics for large numbers of molecules.

provenance.evidence_detail: Pitfall 'Energy-shell vs full Hilbert space' warns against summing over all states with Ω = dim H.
provenance.discriminates: Catches responses that write the microcanonical ensemble as proportional to the identity over the full Hilbert space.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Energy-shell restriction is essential; 0.50 discrimination, merged with pitfall 19.

validation.gold_why: Does not apply uniform distribution over full Hilbert space.

items.title: Canonical ensemble derivation
items.description: The canonical ensemble ρ_can = e^{-βH}/Z with Z = Tr(e^{-βH}) and β = 1/(k_B T) is derived by tracing out a weakly coupled bath from the total system, connecting quantum postulates to statistical mechanics principles.

provenance.evidence_detail: Rollouts agreed the canonical ensemble is derived by tracing out a weakly coupled bath, giving ρ_can = e^{-βH}/Z.
provenance.discriminates: Catches responses that assert the canonical ensemble without deriving it from system–bath weak coupling and partial trace.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Key ensemble derivation; 0.50 discrimination, central to connecting quantum to statistical.

validation.gold_why: No canonical ensemble derivation.

items.title: Many-body Hamiltonian structure

provenance.discriminates: A response that gives only the first and last terms without showing that the phase factor sits between them and cancels.
provenance.calibration_rationale: 2/2 discrimination: complete derivation chain showing time-independence; gold=FAIL but essential to a valid proof.

validation.gold_why: Intermediate chain with phase factor omitted; skips to final result.

items.title: Final expression boxed
items.description: The response states the final probability expression P(E_k, t) = |⟨E_k|ψ(0)⟩|² (or |⟨k|ψ(0)⟩|²) and presents it in a boxed expression.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (b) target is the time-independent expression; the reference answer boxes |⟨E_k|ψ(0)⟩|².
provenance.discriminates: A response that concludes verbally without writing the explicit final probability formula.
provenance.calibration_rationale: 2/2 discrimination and gold=pass: the boxed final result the question asks to derive.

validation.gold_why: Final expression |⟨E_k|ψ(0)⟩|² is boxed.

items.title: Concludes time-independent
items.description: The response explicitly concludes that the probability expression is independent of time, either by stating dP(E_k,t)/dt = 0 or by declaring that no time-dependent factor survives.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (b) asks to show the expression is independent of time; the final conclusion must be stated explicitly.
provenance.discriminates: A response that derives |⟨k|ψ(0)⟩|² but never states that this means the probability is time-independent.
provenance.calibration_rationale: 2/2 discrimination and gold=pass: the explicit conclusion the question demands.

validation.gold_why: Equality chain ends with no time-dependent factor surviving.

items.title: General initial state
items.description: The response carries out the derivation for a general initial state |ψ(0)⟩ using the time-evolution operator, obtaining an expression for the probability of the particular energy eigenvalue, not only for the special case |ψ(0)⟩ = |k⟩.

provenance.evidence_detail: The eigenstate-only proof pitfall (severity medium) warns against proving the result only for the trivial case |ψ(0)⟩ = |k⟩.
provenance.discriminates: A response that proves P = 1 for |ψ(0)⟩ = |k⟩ and generalizes without showing the derivation for an arbitrary state.
provenance.calibration_rationale: 1/2 discrimination and gold=pass: prevents trivial special-case derivation; key to answering generally.

validation.gold_why: Expression uses general |ψ(0)⟩, not special case.

items.title: Avoids amplitude-as-probability
items.description: Avoids stating the probability as the unsquared amplitude e^{-iE_k t/ℏ}⟨k|ψ(0)⟩, instead taking the modulus squared of the full amplitude.

provenance.evidence_detail: The 'Amplitude vs probability' pitfall (severity high) identifies the mistake of stopping at the amplitude and treating its phase as residual time dependence.
provenance.discriminates: A response that computes the amplitude with its time-dependent phase and concludes the probability is time-dependent because the phase survives.
provenance.calibration_rationale: 1/2 discrimination and gold=pass: catches a specific algebraic error observed in flawed responses.

validation.gold_why: Uses modulus squared throughout, not unsquared amplitude.

items.title: Spectral decomposition
items.description: The response uses the spectral decomposition of the time-evolution operator U(t) = Σ_n e^{-iE_n t/ℏ}|n⟩⟨n| with orthonormality ⟨k|n⟩ = δ_{kn} to evaluate ⟨k|U(t)|ψ(0)⟩, obtaining an expression for the probability of the particular energy eigenvalue.

provenance.evidence_detail: Rollout 3 uses spectral decomposition while rollouts 1 and 2 use the direct bra eigenstate property; both methods are valid.
provenance.discriminates: Does not catch a wrong response; this is an alternative valid method that adds depth.
provenance.calibration_rationale: 2/2 discrimination: alternative valid method for evaluating the matrix element; adds real depth.

validation.gold_why: Spectral decomposition not used.

items.title: H time-independent implies commutation
items.description: The response notes that because the Hamiltonian of the system is time-independent, U(t) commutes with H (i.e., [H, U(t)] = 0), which allows |k⟩ to be an eigenstate of U(t).

provenance.evidence_detail: The 'Dropping time-independence of H' pitfall notes that [H,U(t)]=0 is the load-bearing consequence of H being time-independent.
provenance.discriminates: A response that writes e^{-iE_k t/ℏ} as the eigenvalue without any indication of why H and U(t) share eigenstates.
provenance.calibration_rationale: 2/2 discrimination from source 21: connects time-independent H to U(t) eigenstate property.

validation.gold_why: [H,U(t)]=0 not mentioned.

items.title: Avoids skipping U(t)
items.description: Avoids proving time-independence solely via the Schrödinger equation d|ψ⟩/dt = -(i/ℏ)H|ψ⟩ without writing the probability expression |⟨k|U(t)|ψ(0)⟩|² or the relation |ψ(t)⟩ = U(t)|ψ(0)⟩.

provenance.evidence_detail: The 'Skipping U(t) usage' pitfall (severity medium) warns that the question explicitly requires using the time-evolution operator U(t).
provenance.discriminates: A response that reaches the correct final answer by differentiating the Schrödinger equation directly, never exhibiting U(t) in the probability expression.
provenance.calibration_rationale: 0/2 discrimination but guards the question's explicit requirement to use the time-evolution operator.

validation.gold_why: Includes |⟨E_k|U(t)|ψ(0)⟩|², does not skip U(t).

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Propagating V/V typo' (severity high): the reference answer visibly contains '(V/V + 1/T)' as a typo; a solver trusting it verbatim gets ~100 instead of 1488.
provenance.discriminates: A response that copies the reference's V/V typo, yielding ~100 instead of 1488.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Specific observed trap; naming wrong value keeps it checkable.

validation.gold_why: Reference writes V/V instead of u/V symbolically

items.title: Avoids premature rounding
items.description: Avoids truncating frac{5}{75} to 0.06 or otherwise rounding frac{5}{75} + frac{1}{1800} before addition, which would shift the steady-state concentration away from 1488 molecules/cm³.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Arithmetic in denominator' (severity medium): using 0.06 + 0.00056 = 0.06056 gives ~1651 instead of 1488.
provenance.discriminates: A response that rounds 5/75 to 0.06 before adding 1/1800, yielding ~1651 instead of 1488.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Real computational pitfall; 0/3 measured but low weight, kept for coverage.

validation.gold_why: No premature rounding; shows exact fractions

items.title: Average Br2 mass

items.title: Remaining mass final value
items.description: States the remaining mass of CO left as 233.5 mg or 0.2335 g.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (a) asks for remaining mass in grams; reference gives 233.5 mg = 0.2335 g.
provenance.discriminates: A response that reports the removed mass, the wrong subtraction, or a unit-mismatched value as the mass left.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 2/2 negatives, discrimination 1.0; one of the two requested final answers.

validation.gold_why: States 233.5 mg remaining.

items.title: Subtraction step
items.description: Performs the subtraction 280 mg − 46.5 mg = 233.5 mg (or equivalently 0.280 g − 0.0465 g = 0.2335 g).

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference explicitly computes CO left = 280 − 46.5 = 233.5 mg.
provenance.discriminates: A response that adds instead of subtracts, or that skips the subtraction and reports the removed mass as the answer.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 2/2 negatives, discrimination 1.0; core arithmetic step producing the remaining mass.

validation.gold_why: Performs 280 − 46.5 = 233.5 mg.

items.title: Remaining moles final value
items.description: States the remaining moles of CO left as 8.34 × 10^-3 mol.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (b) asks for remaining moles; reference gives 8.34 × 10^-3 mol.
provenance.discriminates: A response that reports moles removed (1.66 × 10^-3) instead of moles left, or omits the mole answer entirely.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 2/2 negatives, discrimination 1.0; the second requested final answer.

validation.gold_why: States 8.34×10^-3 mol remaining.

items.title: Final mole calculation
items.description: Computes moles left by dividing the remaining mass 233.5 × 10^-3 g by the molar mass 28 g/mol, obtaining 8.34 × 10^-3 mol.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference calculates moles left = (233.5 × 10^-3)/28 = 8.34 × 10^-3.
provenance.discriminates: A response that gives the correct mole answer but does not show the mass-divided-by-molar-mass computation for the remaining sample.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 2/2 negatives, discrimination 1.0; shows the method yielding the final mole value.

items.title: Mole formula statement
items.description: States that the moles of CO left are calculated as weight divided by molar mass (wt./m. wt.).

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference uses the notation moles = wt./m. wt. = (233.5 × 10^-3)/28.
provenance.discriminates: A response that obtains moles left by subtracting moles removed from initial moles without ever relating mass to moles via wt./m. wt.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 1/2 negatives, discrimination 0.50; adds methodological clarity for the mole calculation.

validation.gold_why: States moles = wt./m. wt.

items.title: Both quantities reported
items.description: Reports both the remaining mass of CO left in grams and the remaining moles left.

provenance.evidence_detail: The question asks 'How many g and mole of CO are left?' — two separate deliverables.
provenance.discriminates: A response that computes only mass or only moles and leaves the other blank.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 0/2 negatives but ensures both sub-questions are answered; essential for completeness.

validation.gold_why: Reports both remaining mass and moles.

items.title: Avoids unit-mismatch subtraction
items.description: Avoids subtracting the removed mass in grams (4.65 × 10^-2 g) from the initial 280 mg without first converting both quantities to the same unit.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'mg/g mismatch in subtraction' (severity high): computing 280 − 0.0465 gives ≈ 280, ignoring the removed mass.
provenance.discriminates: A response that computes 280 − 0.0465 ≈ 280 and reports the mass left as approximately 280 mg or 280 g.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 2/2 negatives, discrimination 1.0; most common observed arithmetic trap in this problem.

validation.gold_why: Subtracts in same units (mg).

items.title: Avoids reporting removed as left
items.description: Avoids reporting the mass of CO removed (4.65 × 10^-2 g or 46.5 mg) as the mass of CO left.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Stopped at removed mass' (severity high): presenting the removed quantity as the final answer.
provenance.discriminates: A response that gives 4.65 × 10^-2 g or 46.5 mg as the mass of CO left.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 0/2 negatives but names a conceptual trap where removed mass is mistaken for remaining mass.

validation.gold_why: Reports 233.5 mg as remaining, not removed.

items.title: Avoids reversed subtraction
items.description: Avoids adding the removed mass (46.5 mg) to the initial 280 mg instead of subtracting it to find the mass left.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Subtraction direction reversed' (severity medium): 280 + 46.5 = 326.5 mg, which exceeds the initial mass.
provenance.discriminates: A response that reports 326.5 mg or 0.3265 g as the mass left.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 0/2 negatives but identifies a sign-error trap in the subtraction step for 280 mg.

validation.gold_why: Subtracts removed mass, does not add.

validation_summary.pitfall_weight_convention: stored on the RaR -1/-2 scale by schema.Criterion; graded by magnitude with polarity=positive

items.title: Selects option D
items.description: The response selects option (D), stating that the slope of the kinetic energy versus frequency plot is the same for all metals and independent of the intensity of the radiation.

provenance.evidence_detail: The question's single labelled sub-question requires identifying the correct multiple-choice option, and the reference answer states Ans. D.
provenance.discriminates: A response that selects (A), (B), or (C) instead of (D).
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 2/2 negatives; the correct option is the core answer.

validation.gold_why: States 'Ans. D' explicitly.

items.title: Slope equals h
items.description: The response identifies the slope of the kinetic energy versus frequency plot as Planck's constant h.

provenance.evidence_detail: The consensus among attempts was that the slope of KE vs ν is h, while the reference framed it via stopping potential as h/e; the question specifies KE on the y-axis so slope = h.
provenance.discriminates: A response that quotes the slope as h/e when the question asks about kinetic energy, not stopping potential.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 2/2 negatives; slope = h is essential for the KE plot asked.

validation.gold_why: Gives slope as h/e, not h, for V0 plot.

items.title: Photon energy E = hν
items.description: The response relates the slope to the photon energy E = hν, explaining that each photon's energy increment per unit frequency is Planck's constant h.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference uses the relation between photon energy and frequency via the photoelectric equation.
provenance.discriminates: A response that gives no physical basis for why the slope equals h.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 2/2 negatives; provides the physical justification for slope = h.

validation.gold_why: Does not relate slope to photon energy E = hν.

items.title: Slope same for all metals
items.description: The response states that the slope is the same for all metals, regardless of the nature of the metal used.

provenance.evidence_detail: Option (D) explicitly states the slope is the same for all metals, and the reference confirms this.
provenance.discriminates: A response that claims the slope varies with the metal used.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Sources caught 2/2 and 1/2 negatives; directly answers the metal-dependence sub-question.

validation.gold_why: Says 'same for all metals' and 'universal constant.'

items.title: h is universal constant
items.description: The response explicitly describes Planck's constant h as a universal constant that does not vary with the metal used.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference answer describes the slope as h/e and calls it a universal constant.
provenance.discriminates: A response that treats h as a material-specific parameter.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 1/2 negatives; explains why the slope is metal-independent.

validation.gold_why: Describes slope as 'a universal constant.'

items.title: Slope independent of intensity
items.description: The response states that the slope is independent of the intensity of the incident radiation.

provenance.evidence_detail: The high-severity mined pitfall 'Intensity affects KE' leads students to select option (B) or (C).
provenance.discriminates: A response that selects (B) or (C) or states the slope changes with radiation intensity.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Sources caught 1/2 negatives each; directly addresses the intensity sub-question.

validation.gold_why: States slope is independent of intensity.

items.title: Work function sets intercept
items.description: The response states that the work function φ determines the intercept (−φ) of the kinetic energy versus frequency line, not the slope.

provenance.evidence_detail: The mined pitfall 'Slope vs intercept confusion' notes students wrongly attribute φ's metal-dependence to the slope rather than the intercept.
provenance.discriminates: A response that says the work function changes the slope for different metals.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 1/2 negatives; distinguishes intercept from slope, gold=FAIL so weighted low.

validation.gold_why: Shows φ/e in equation but doesn't state it determines intercept.

items.title: Intensity affects count not KE
items.description: The response states that the intensity of the incident radiation affects the number of emitted photoelectrons, not their maximum kinetic energy.

provenance.evidence_detail: The mined pitfall 'Intensity affects KE' identifies the temptation to claim intensity changes KE_max.
provenance.discriminates: A response that says brighter radiation increases the kinetic energy of emitted photoelectrons.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 1/2 negatives; adds physical depth on intensity's role.

validation.gold_why: Does not mention intensity affecting photoelectron count.

items.title: Avoids threshold-frequency error
items.description: Avoids conflating the threshold frequency ν₀ = φ/h, the x-intercept of the line, with a metal-dependent slope.

provenance.evidence_detail: The mined pitfall 'Threshold frequency misread as slope' describes students treating ν₀ as evidence that the slope varies with metal.
provenance.discriminates: A response that argues the slope changes with metal because the threshold frequency changes.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 1/2 negatives; names the specific threshold-frequency conflation trap.

validation.gold_why: No conflation of threshold frequency with slope.

items.title: Avoids classical reasoning
items.description: Avoids applying classical wave intuition that the kinetic energy of emitted photoelectrons is proportional to the intensity of the incident radiation.

provenance.evidence_detail: The mined pitfall 'Classical proportionality to intensity' identifies this as leading to option (C).
provenance.discriminates: A response that uses classical wave theory to argue KE increases with intensity and thus selects (C).
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 1/2 negatives; targets the classical-intensity misconception observed in flawed responses.

validation.gold_why: No classical wave intuition about KE and intensity.

items.title: Names ovarian carcinoma
items.description: The response identifies ovarian carcinoma as the most likely diagnosis rather than stopping at ascites or abdominal distension as the final answer.

provenance.evidence_detail: The question asks for the single most likely diagnosis; the reference answer states ovarian carcinoma.
provenance.discriminates: Responses that name cirrhosis, pregnancy, Meigs syndrome, endometrial cancer, or ascites alone instead of ovarian carcinoma.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Core diagnosis; caught 2/2 negatives, discrimination 1.00.

validation.gold_why: Identifies ovarian carcinoma as most likely diagnosis.

items.title: Ascites without liver/heart disease
items.description: The response states that ascites is present without other signs of liver disease or cardiovascular issues, focusing on an abdominal etiology such as ovarian cancer.

provenance.evidence_detail: Consensus that no stigmata of cirrhosis or cardiopulmonary signs are present, making ovarian carcinoma more appropriate.
provenance.discriminates: Responses that do not address why common ascites causes (cirrhosis, CHF) are excluded.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Key reasoning path; caught 2/2 negatives, discrimination 1.00.

validation.gold_why: Notes absence of liver/heart signs, redirects to abdominal etiology.

items.title: GI symptoms support malignancy
items.description: The response connects the intermittent constipation and abdominal bloating to ovarian carcinoma as known vague, non-specific symptoms of an ovarian tumor.

provenance.evidence_detail: Consensus that vague GI symptoms (constipation, bloating) support ovarian malignancy rather than a primary GI disorder.
provenance.discriminates: Responses that treat constipation as an isolated GI problem unconnected to the ovarian diagnosis.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Links non-specific symptoms to diagnosis; caught 2/2 negatives, discrimination 1.00.

validation.gold_why: Connects constipation and bloating to ovarian tumor symptoms.

items.title: Weight gain linked to tumor
items.description: The response connects the recent weight gain and abdominal distension to the presence of an ovarian tumor causing ascites.

provenance.evidence_detail: Consensus that weight gain plus distension in a postmenopausal woman points to ovarian malignancy rather than a benign process.
provenance.discriminates: Responses that treat weight gain as an unrelated or lifestyle finding.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Integrates key presenting symptom; caught 2/2 negatives, discrimination 1.00.

validation.gold_why: Links weight gain and distension to ovarian tumor causing ascites.

items.title: Postmenopausal status
items.description: The response identifies the patient as postmenopausal based on last menstrual period 8 months ago and age 54.

provenance.evidence_detail: Consensus across all rollouts that menopausal status is a key supporting feature for ovarian carcinoma.
provenance.discriminates: Responses that interpret the 8-month amenorrhea as pregnancy-related rather than menopause.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Necessary epidemiologic context; caught 1/2 negatives, discrimination 0.50.

validation.gold_why: States she is postmenopausal.

items.title: Fluid wave as ascites
items.description: The response interprets the abdominal fluid wave as indicating ascites.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts and the reference agree the fluid wave signifies ascites; failing to make this link breaks the diagnostic chain.
provenance.discriminates: Responses that describe the fluid wave as a separate finding without connecting it to ascites.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Required intermediate finding; caught 0/2 but conceptually necessary for the diagnosis.

validation.gold_why: States 'ascites (abdominal fluid wave)' explicitly.

items.title: Negative b-hCG excludes pregnancy
items.description: The response cites the negative b-hCG result as excluding pregnancy, supporting the menopausal interpretation.

provenance.evidence_detail: Consensus across all rollouts that the negative β-hCG rules out pregnancy.
provenance.discriminates: Responses that ignore the β-hCG result and leave pregnancy in the differential.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Gold=FAIL but genuinely necessary; caught 1/2 negatives, discrimination 0.50.

validation.gold_why: Does not explicitly cite the negative b-hCG result.

items.title: Normal electrolytes noted
items.description: The response references the normal electrolyte levels as arguing against a metabolic or hepatic cause of the ascites.

provenance.evidence_detail: The question provides normal electrolyte levels as an explicit given; consensus rollouts used this to exclude metabolic disturbance.
provenance.discriminates: Responses that ignore the normal electrolyte finding when building the differential.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Gold=FAIL but high discrimination; caught 2/2 negatives, kept low weight.

validation.gold_why: Does not reference normal electrolyte levels.

items.title: Serous subtype mentioned
items.description: The response mentions serous as a potential histologic subtype of the ovarian carcinoma.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference answer specifies 'potentially a serous type,' which no rollout included.
provenance.discriminates: Responses that stop at 'epithelial ovarian carcinoma' without noting the most common subtype.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Added depth from reference; caught 2/2 negatives, discrimination 1.00.

validation.gold_why: Mentions 'potentially a serous type.'

items.title: Further evaluation suggested
items.description: The response mentions the need for further evaluation including imaging and possibly a referral to a specialist to confirm the diagnosis.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference answer states further evaluation including imaging and specialist referral would be needed; no rollout mentioned next steps.
provenance.discriminates: Responses that give only a diagnosis without acknowledging that confirmation requires additional workup.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Real added depth; caught 0/2 negatives, low priority.

validation.gold_why: Mentions imaging and specialist referral to confirm.

items.title: Avoids cirrhosis or heart failure
items.description: Avoids diagnosing cirrhosis, hepatic decompensation, or heart failure as the cause of ascites, given the absence of liver disease stigmata, cardiovascular signs, and normal electrolyte levels.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Cirrhosis as default ascites' — high severity; cirrhosis is the reflexive default but no jaundice, spider angiomata, or abnormal electrolytes are present.
provenance.discriminates: Responses that default to cirrhotic ascites without considering ovarian malignancy.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Plausible distractor; caught 1/2 negatives across merged sources, discrimination 0.50.

validation.gold_why: Does not diagnose cirrhosis; notes absence of liver signs.

items.title: Avoids endometrial carcinoma
items.description: Avoids diagnosing endometrial carcinoma, which classically presents with abnormal vaginal bleeding that this patient explicitly denies.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Endometrial cancer instead' notes that the absence of vaginal bleeding is the key discriminator; the question explicitly states the patient denies abnormal bleeding.
provenance.discriminates: Responses that do not use the absence of vaginal bleeding to rule out endometrial cancer.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Specific trap given vaginal bleeding denial; caught 1/2 via source 20, discrimination 0.50.

validation.gold_why: Does not note denial of abnormal vaginal bleeding.

items.title: Avoids benign ovarian cyst
items.description: Avoids diagnosing a benign or functional ovarian cyst, given that ascites in a postmenopausal woman strongly favors ovarian carcinoma.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Benign ovarian cyst' — low severity; ascites and age make malignancy far more likely.
provenance.discriminates: Responses that settle on a benign cyst instead of carcinoma.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Common misdiagnosis trap; caught 0/2 but names a specific wrong move relevant to this case.

validation.gold_why: Does not diagnose benign ovarian cyst.

items.title: σ_x matrix
items.description: The response states that the Pauli matrix σ_x (or σ_1) equals the 2x2 matrix begin pmatrix 0 & 1 \ 1 & 0 end pmatrix.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (a) requires explicit Pauli matrices; reference answer lists σ_x = [[0,1],[1,0]].
provenance.discriminates: A response that gives a wrong off-diagonal sign or swaps entries in σ_x.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Core requested quantity; gold passed. Low discrimination but essential to correctness.

validation.gold_why: σ_x explicitly given as correct matrix.

items.title: σ_y matrix
items.description: The response states that the Pauli matrix σ_y (or σ_2) equals the 2x2 matrix begin pmatrix 0 & -i \ i & 0 end pmatrix, with −i upper-right and +i lower-left so that the matrix is Hermitian.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'σ_y sign flipped': writing σ_y = [[0,i],[-i,0]] which is anti-Hermitian.
provenance.discriminates: A response that swaps the i entries and produces an anti-Hermitian σ_y.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Core requested quantity; caught a sign-flip negative. Highest discrimination among the three matrices.

validation.gold_why: σ_y has −i upper-right, +i lower-left.

items.title: σ_z matrix
items.description: The response states that the Pauli matrix σ_z (or σ_3) equals the 2x2 matrix begin pmatrix 1 & 0 \ 0 & -1 end pmatrix.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (a) requires explicit Pauli matrices; reference answer lists σ_z = [[1,0],[0,-1]].
provenance.discriminates: A response that gives σ_z = [[1,0],[0,1]] or flips the diagonal signs.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Core requested quantity; gold passed. Essential despite zero measured discrimination.

validation.gold_why: σ_z explicitly given as correct matrix.

items.title: Two values → 2D space
items.description: The response argues from the assumption that measuring electron spin yields one of two values that the spin Hilbert space has dimension two, so operators are represented by 2x2 matrices.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (a) asks to start from the two-outcome assumption; consensus_correct includes 'Two measurement outcomes imply 2D Hilbert space'.
provenance.discriminates: A response that simply states the matrices without connecting them to the two-outcome assumption.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Foundational starting point for the derivation; gold=FAIL but genuinely necessary to the answer's logic.

validation.gold_why: No argument from two values to 2D space.

items.title: S = (ħ/2)σ relation
items.description: The response states the spin operator relation S_i = (ħ/2)σ_i for i = x, y, z, including the proportionality constant ħ/2 rather than identifying S directly with σ.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Missing ħ/2 factor': writing S = σ gives eigenvalues ±1 instead of ±ħ/2.
provenance.discriminates: A response that writes S = σ and claims spin eigenvalues are ±1.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught a negative that omitted ħ/2; disc=0.50. Load-bearing relation between spin operator and Pauli matrices.

validation.gold_why: ħ/2 factor not mentioned in any relation.

items.title: Eigenvalues ±ħ/2
items.description: The response states that the two spin measurement values are ±ħ/2, equivalently that the eigenvalues of each Pauli matrix σ_i are ±1.

provenance.evidence_detail: Implicit constraint: electron is spin-1/2 so two measurement values are ±ħ/2; consensus_correct includes this.
provenance.discriminates: A response that claims the eigenvalues are ±1 without the ħ/2 physical rescaling, or omits the eigenvalue connection entirely.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Gold=FAIL, disc=0, but necessary to connect the two-value assumption to the matrix derivation.

validation.gold_why: Eigenvalues ±ħ/2 or ±1 not mentioned.

items.title: Hermiticity of spin operator
items.description: The response states that each spin component operator S_i is a 2x2 Hermitian matrix satisfying S_i† = S_i.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (b) asks to show the spin operator is a 2x2 Hermitian matrix; consensus_correct includes σ_i†=σ_i.
provenance.discriminates: A response that does not impose or mention Hermiticity as a constraint on the spin operator.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Explicitly requested in the question; gold=FAIL but genuinely necessary and verifiable from the response.

validation.gold_why: Hermiticity of S_i not mentioned.

items.title: Traceless constraint
items.description: The response imposes Tr(σ_i) = 0 as a constraint on the Pauli matrices, noting that the two eigenvalues ±1 sum to zero.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Missing traceless constraint': forgetting Tr(A)=0 leaves the derivation under-constrained.
provenance.discriminates: A response that parameterizes a general Hermitian matrix with arbitrary independent diagonal entries a, b without forcing b = −a.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught a negative; disc=0.50. Key derivation constraint that narrows the matrix ansatz.

validation.gold_why: Tracelessness constraint not mentioned.

items.title: σ² = I property
items.description: The response states or uses the property that each Pauli matrix squares to the identity, σ_i² = I.

provenance.evidence_detail: Consensus_correct includes 'σ_i² = I'; this is a load-bearing constraint in the derivation from eigenvalues ±1.
provenance.discriminates: A response that derives the matrices without using the A²=I condition that follows from two opposite eigenvalues.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught a negative; disc=0.50. Essential algebraic constraint used to derive or verify the matrices.

validation.gold_why: σ_i² = I property not stated.

items.title: Pauli commutation relations
items.description: The response uses the commutation relation [σ_i, σ_j] = 2i ε_ijk σ_k (equivalently [S_i, S_j] = iħ ε_ijk S_k) to derive or constrain the Pauli matrices.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Wrong commutator normalization': using iε_ijk σ_k instead of 2iε_ijk σ_k.
provenance.discriminates: A response that carries over [J_i,J_j]=iħJ_k directly to σ without the factor-of-2 from the ħ/2 rescaling.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Absorbed pitfall avoiding the missing factor of 2; disc=0.50. Constrains σ_x and σ_y from σ_z.

validation.gold_why: No commutator relation stated at all.

items.title: Identity in Pauli basis
items.description: The response states that the set {I, σ_x, σ_y, σ_z}, including the identity matrix, forms a basis for the space of all 2x2 matrices.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (c) target: proof that {I, σx, σy, σz} spans all 2x2 matrices; consensus_correct includes this.
provenance.discriminates: A response that claims {σ_x, σ_y, σ_z} alone spans all 2x2 matrices, omitting the identity (pitfall: 'Identity omitted from basis').
provenance.calibration_rationale: Directly answers the basis sub-question; gold=FAIL but genuinely necessary to the answer's correctness.

validation.gold_why: Basis including identity not mentioned.

items.title: General expansion formula
items.description: The response writes the general expansion of any 2x2 matrix M as M = a₀ I + a₁ σ_x + a₂ σ_y + a₃ σ_z using the Pauli matrices.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (c) target: any 2x2 matrix decomposes as a₀ I + a·σ; consensus_correct includes this expansion.
provenance.discriminates: A response that asserts the basis property but never writes the explicit expansion formula.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Concrete instantiation of the basis claim; gold=FAIL but needed to show how to write down any matrix.

validation.gold_why: General expansion formula not written.

items.title: Spanning dimension argument
items.description: The response notes that the space of 2x2 complex matrices is 4-dimensional and that four linearly independent matrices {I, σ_x, σ_y, σ_z} therefore span it.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (c) target includes 'completeness/linear-independence justification'; consensus_correct includes the linear independence claim.
provenance.discriminates: A response that states the basis property without any justification of linear independence or dimension counting.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Merged duplicate items; gold=FAIL, disc=0, but provides the mathematical justification for the basis claim.

validation.gold_why: Linear independence not argued.

items.title: Expansion coefficient formula
items.description: The response gives the expansion coefficient formula a_i = (1/2) Tr(σ_i M) for extracting coefficients in the Pauli basis for any 2x2 matrix M.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Expansion coefficient missing 1/2': writing a_i = Tr(σ_i M) without the factor 1/2, since Tr(σ_i σ_j) = 2δ_ij.
provenance.discriminates: A response that gives a_i = Tr(σ_i M), off by a factor of 2.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught both negatives; disc=1.00. Real added depth, though not strictly required for correctness.

validation.gold_why: Expansion coefficient formula not given.

items.title: Hermitian traceless ansatz
items.description: The response writes a general 2x2 Hermitian traceless matrix in the form begin pmatrix a & c* \ c & -a end pmatrix with the constraint a² + |c|² = 1, used as the starting ansatz for deriving the Pauli matrices.

provenance.evidence_detail: Rollout 1 uses this parameterization with a²+|c|²=1; divergent derivation methods both arrive at the same matrices.
provenance.discriminates: A response that never parameterizes the general Hermitian traceless ansatz and thus cannot derive the Pauli form from constraints.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught both negatives; disc=1.00. Provides the intermediate parameterization from which all three matrices follow.

validation.gold_why: General Hermitian parameterization not given.

items.title: Names hyponatremia
items.description: Names hyponatremia as the most likely electrolyte imbalance causing the symptoms of weakness, lassitude, orthostatic hypotension, nausea, and fever in this 55-year-old woman.

validation.gold_why: Explicitly names hyponatremia as the most likely imbalance.

items.title: Scenario favors hyponatremia
items.description: States that the overall clinical scenario more strongly suggests hyponatremia than other electrolyte disturbances.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference answer concludes that the overall clinical scenario more strongly suggests hyponatremia than alternatives such as hypokalemia or hypomagnesemia.
provenance.discriminates: A response that lists hyponatremia among multiple possibilities without stating it is the more strongly suggested diagnosis.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Comparative reasoning; caught 3/3 negatives, discrimination 1.00.

validation.gold_why: States overall clinical scenario more strongly suggests hyponatremia.

items.title: Final answer 0.254 g/L
items.description: States the iodide concentration in the original solution is 0.254 g/L.

items.description: Sets up the equivalence n_eq(iodide) = n_eq(cerium) as the basis for the titration calculation.
