items.title: Amino acid count 480
items.description: The response computes the number of amino acids as 65,760 daltons divided by 137 daltons per amino acid, yielding 480 amino acids.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference answer's first step is 65,760 / 137 = 480 amino acids.
provenance.discriminates: A response that skips the division or uses a wrong divisor producing a different residue count.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Load-bearing intermediate; 0/2 caught but the 480 result is essential to all downstream steps.

validation.gold_why: Divides 65,760 by 137 to get 480 amino acids.

items.title: Triplet multiplication
items.description: The response multiplies the 480 amino acid count by three nucleotides per amino acid to convert residues to mRNA nucleotides, rather than dividing by three.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference answer states 'each codon contains three nucleotides' and multiplies 480 × 3.
provenance.discriminates: A response that reports 480 as the final nucleotide count without applying the triplet factor.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 2/2 negatives; the multiply-by-three step is the core conversion and discriminates perfectly.

validation.gold_why: Multiplies 480 amino acids by 3 nucleotides per amino acid.

items.title: Coding region 1440
items.description: The response states that the coding region of the mRNA is 1,440 nucleotides long, distinguishing it from the total mRNA molecule length.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference answer's final result is 1,440 nucleotides (480 amino acids × 3 nucleotides per amino acid).
provenance.discriminates: A response that gives 480, 160, 1,443, or any other value as the final nucleotide count.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 2/2 negatives from both sources; final answer plus coding-region specificity, top discriminative power.

validation.gold_why: States coding region is 1440 nucleotides long.

items.title: 137 as divisor
items.description: The response divides the 65,760 dalton polypeptide mass by 137 daltons per amino acid as the average residue mass.

provenance.evidence_detail: The water-loss mass correction pitfall warns against adjusting 137 Da downward to ~119 Da; the reference uses 137 directly.
provenance.discriminates: A response that subtracts ~18 Da for water loss and uses ~119 Da as the divisor, yielding ~553 residues.
provenance.calibration_rationale: 0/2 caught independently, but selecting the correct divisor is a necessary intermediate for the 480 result.

validation.gold_why: Uses 137 as divisor, not a water-loss-corrected value.

items.title: Equal composition justification
items.description: The response uses the stated assumption that the polypeptide contains equal amounts of all 20 common amino acids to justify applying the 137 dalton average directly.

provenance.evidence_detail: The consensus_correct section notes that the equal-composition assumption validates using 137 Da as the mean residue mass.
provenance.discriminates: A response that ignores the assumption or argues the average mass cannot be applied without sequence information.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 2/2 negatives; the equal-amounts assumption is what licenses the 137 average and discriminates well.

validation.gold_why: References 'this assumption' and applies 137 dalton average directly.

items.title: Avoids water-loss correction
items.description: Avoids subtracting water mass from the 137 dalton average amino acid mass before dividing 65,760 by it.

provenance.evidence_detail: The water-loss mass correction pitfall describes adjusting 137 Da to ~119 Da as a medium-severity mistake.
provenance.discriminates: A response that uses 119 Da or similar corrected value and obtains ~553 residues and ~1,659 nucleotides.
provenance.calibration_rationale: 0/2 caught; not a near-duplicate of item 4 since a wrong non-water-corrected divisor can still fail 4 only.

validation.gold_why: No water-loss correction applied before dividing.

items.title: Avoids 480 as mRNA length
items.description: Avoids presenting 480 as the mRNA length without specifying the relation to nucleotide count.

provenance.evidence_detail: The residue count as answer pitfall describes stopping at 480 and presenting it as the final length.
provenance.discriminates: A response whose final stated mRNA length is 480 with no nucleotide conversion.
provenance.calibration_rationale: 0/2 caught; not a near-duplicate of item 3 since item 3 is about the correct coding region length while this is about conflating amino acids with nucleotides.

validation.gold_why: 480 is clearly labeled as amino acid count, not mRNA length.

items.title: Equal composition justification
items.description: The response uses the stated assumption that the polypeptide contains equal amounts of all 20 amino acids to justify applying the 137 dalton average directly.

provenance.evidence_detail: The consensus_correct section notes that the equal-composition assumption validates using 137 Da as the mean residue mass.
provenance.discriminates: A response that ignores the assumption or argues the average mass cannot be applied without sequence information.

validation.gold_why: References 'this assumption' and applies 137 dalton average directly.

items.title: Final dS formula
items.description: The response states the final result \(dS = \frac{dV_B}{T}(P_B - P_A)\) for the two-compartment system, with the common temperature \(T\) appearing explicitly in the denominator.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (a) target is the stated expression for dS.
provenance.discriminates: A response that derives an intermediate but never writes the target expression, or writes a sign-flipped version such as \((P_A - P_B)\).
provenance.calibration_rationale: Core requested result; caught 2/2 negatives, discrimination 1.00.

validation.gold_why: Final result stated explicitly.

items.title: Volume conservation constraint
items.description: The response uses the isolated-system constraint \(dV_A = -dV_B\) for the flexible wall separating the two subsystems, avoiding the wrong move of setting \(dV_A = +dV_B\).

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall: Volume conservation sign yields a spurious pressure-sum term.
provenance.discriminates: A response that writes \(dV_A = dV_B\) and cannot reach the target expression.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Load-bearing constraint; caught 1/2 negatives, discrimination 0.50.

validation.gold_why: Uses dV_A = -dV_B.

items.title: Energy conservation constraint
items.description: The response applies the isolated condition \(dU_A = -dU_B\) for the two-compartment system so that the internal-energy terms cancel in the entropy differential.

provenance.evidence_detail: All correct rollouts enforced conservation of total internal energy.
provenance.discriminates: A response that leaves a spurious \(dU_A + dU_B\) term in the entropy expression.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Required intermediate; discrimination 0.00 but essential for cancellation.

validation.gold_why: dU_A = -dU_B applied.

items.title: Equal temperatures used
items.description: The response uses \(T_A = T_B = T\) for the two subsystems having the same temperature, enabling the pressure-driven entropy expression to emerge.

provenance.evidence_detail: All correct rollouts set the common temperature before simplifying dS.
provenance.discriminates: A response that keeps separate \(T_A, T_B\) and cannot reduce to the single-T form.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Necessary assumption; discrimination 0.00 but correctness depends on it.

validation.gold_why: T_A = T_B stated.

items.title: Per-compartment entropy relation
items.description: The response writes \(dS_i = \frac{1}{T}(dU_i + P_i\,dV_i)\) or the equivalent for each compartment, connecting entropy change to internal energy and volume.

provenance.evidence_detail: All correct rollouts began from this fundamental relation for each subsystem.
provenance.discriminates: A response that uses a wrong sign, e.g. \(dS_i = (1/T)(dU_i - P_i dV_i)\).
provenance.calibration_rationale: Key intermediate step; caught 1/2 negatives, discrimination 0.50.

validation.gold_why: Per-subsystem entropy relation written.

items.title: First-law heat expression
items.description: The response writes \(\delta q_A = dU_A + P_A\,dV_A\) and \(\delta q_B = dU_B + P_B\,dV_B\) via the First Law before forming the entropy expression.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference uses the First Law and δq/T path rather than jumping to the fundamental relation.
provenance.discriminates: A response that omits the explicit First-Law heat terms but still reaches the formula correctly.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Derivation step from reference; caught 1/2 negatives, discrimination 0.50.

validation.gold_why: First-law heat expressions written.

items.title: Interpretation P_B > P_A
items.description: The response states that when \(P_B > P_A\), \(dV_B\) is positive because compartment B will expand, consistent with the entropy of the isolated system increasing.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (b) requires the sign of dV_B when P_B > P_A.
provenance.discriminates: A response that claims B contracts when its pressure is higher.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Requested sub-question; caught 1/2 negatives, discrimination 0.50.

validation.gold_why: States dV_B positive when P_B > P_A.

items.title: Interpretation P_B < P_A
items.description: The response states that when \(P_B < P_A\), \(dV_B\) is negative because compartment A expands, avoiding the reversed interpretation that would tie expansion to the lower pressure.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall: Reversed physical interpretation of the sign of dV_B.
provenance.discriminates: A response with the correct formula but a backwards direction of expansion.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Requested sub-question; caught 2/2 negatives, discrimination 1.00.

validation.gold_why: Interpretation ties expansion to larger pressure.

items.title: Second-law justification
items.description: The response justifies the sign of \(dV_B\) in each case by invoking the Second Law so that \(dS \geq 0\) for the isolated system, keeping the sign consistent with \((P_B - P_A)\).

provenance.evidence_detail: Divergence on strict vs non-strict inequality; the reference requires the sign to follow from dS positivity.
provenance.discriminates: A response whose stated signs of \(dV_B\) would make dS negative for a spontaneous process.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Logical anchor for interpretation; combined sources caught 2/2 negatives.

validation.gold_why: Sign of dV_B consistent with dS > 0.

items.title: Avoid reversed work sign
items.description: Avoids writing \(\delta q = dU - P\,dV\) with reversed sign; the response uses \(\delta q = dU + P\,dV\) so that \(dS = \frac{dV_B}{T}(P_B - P_A)\) rather than \((P_A - P_B)\).

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall: Work sign convention produces a sign-reversed pressure difference.
provenance.discriminates: A response that uses the opposite work convention and obtains \(dS = (dV_B/T)(P_A - P_B)\).
provenance.calibration_rationale: Specific sign trap; caught 1/2 negatives, discrimination 0.50.

validation.gold_why: Uses δq = dU + P dV.

items.title: Avoid spurious heat term
items.description: Avoids introducing an extra heat-transfer entropy term across the wall; the response uses the equal temperature to leave only the pressure-driven volume term in the system's \(dS\).

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall: Equal-T heat term mishandled, adding a spurious δq/T contribution.
provenance.discriminates: A response that adds a heat-exchange entropy term despite equal temperatures.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Plausible but wrong move; discrimination 0.00, low weight.

validation.gold_why: No extra heat-transfer term; equal T used.

items.title: Total entropy as sum
items.description: The response writes the total entropy change of the two-compartment system as \(dS = dS_A + dS_B\) before substituting the per-subsystem relations.

provenance.evidence_detail: All correct rollouts formed the total entropy as the sum of the two subsystem entropies.
provenance.discriminates: A response that treats dS as a single-subsystem quantity rather than the composite system entropy.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Basic structural step; discrimination 0.00, minimal added depth.

validation.gold_why: dS = dS_A + dS_B written.

items.title: No residual dU term
items.description: The final expression for the system's entropy \(dS\) contains no residual \(dU_A\) or \(dU_B\) term, only \(\frac{dV_B}{T}(P_B - P_A)\).

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall: Energy conservation dropped, leaving an undefined dU term.
provenance.discriminates: A response that keeps an uncanceled \(dU_A + dU_B\) contribution in the final formula.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Checks cancellation worked; caught 1/2 negatives, discrimination 0.50.

validation.gold_why: Final expression has no dU terms.

items.title: Pressure difference drives change
items.description: The response states that the direction of volume change is driven by the pressure difference \((P_B - P_A)\) between the two subsystems.

provenance.evidence_detail: All correct rollouts tied the sign of dV_B to the pressure-difference factor.
provenance.discriminates: A response that attributes the volume change to a temperature difference rather than a pressure difference.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Interpretive depth; caught 1/2 negatives, discrimination 0.50.

validation.gold_why: Pressure difference drives volume change implied.

items.title: Names disinhibition diagnosis
items.description: The response states that the presentation is suggestive of disinhibition secondary to benzodiazepines.
